sentences.zh: 【梁紀二】 起旃蒙作噩，盡強圉大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 2] From Zhanmeng Zuoe through Qiangyu Dayuanxian; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 2] From Zhanmeng Zuoe through Qiangyu Dayuanxian—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝二天監四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, the Martial Sovereign, second scroll, fourth year of Tianjian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fourth year of Tianjian (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元五零五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, 505 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, AD 505)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯朔，詔曰：「二漢登賢，莫非經術，服膺雅道，名立行成。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guimao the new moon, an edict said: "In the Two Han dynasties those elevated to office were all men of classical learning; embracing the elegant Way, they established their names through conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guimao the new moon, an edict said: "In the Two Han dynasties, those raised to office were all scholars of the classics; embracing the refined Way, they won renown through their conduct.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉浮蕩，儒教淪歇，風節罔樹，抑此之由。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin were frivolous; Confucian teaching declined and moral integrity was not cultivated—this was the cause of suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin grew dissolute; Confucian teaching fell into decay and moral integrity was no longer cultivated—and this was why.

sentences.zh: 可置《五經》博士各一人，廣開館宇，招內後進。」

translations.literal: Let one Erudite for each of the Five Classics be appointed, broadly open academies, and recruit promising students within."
translations.idiomatic: Let one Erudite for each of the Five Classics be appointed, open academies on a broad scale, and recruit promising students from within the realm."

sentences.zh: 於是以賀瑒及平原明山賓、吳興沈峻、建平嚴植之補博士，各主一館，館有數百生，給其餼廩，其射策通明者即除為吏，期年之間，懷經負笈者雲會。

translations.literal: Thereupon He Chang and Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan, Shen Jun of Wuxing, and Yan Zhizhi of Jianping were appointed as Erudites; each headed one academy, with several hundred students per academy, supplied with stipends and grain; those who excelled in the archery-board examination were immediately appointed as officials. Within a year, those bearing classics on their backs gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon He Chang, Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan, Shen Jun of Wuxing, and Yan Zhizhi of Jianping were appointed Erudites; each headed one academy with several hundred students, who received stipends and grain rations. Those who distinguished themselves in the written examination were immediately appointed to office. Within a year, scholars bearing the classics on their backs gathered in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 瑒，循之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Chang was the great-great-grandson of He Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was the great-great-grandson of He Xun.

sentences.zh: 又選學生，往會稽雲門山從何胤受業，命胤選門徒中經明行修者，具以名聞。

translations.literal: Students were also selected to go to Yunmen Mountain in Kuaiji to study under He Yin; the emperor ordered Yin to choose from among his disciples those accomplished in the classics and upright in conduct, and report all their names.
translations.idiomatic: Students were also selected to study under He Yin at Yunmen Mountain in Kuaiji. The emperor ordered Yin to choose from among his disciples those accomplished in the classics and upright in conduct and report all their names.

sentences.zh: 分遣博士祭酒巡州郡立學。

translations.literal: Erudites and Libationers were dispatched separately to tour the provinces and commanderies and establish schools.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites and Libationers were dispatched throughout the provinces and commanderies to establish schools.

sentences.zh: 初，譙國夏侯道遷以輔國將軍從裴叔業鎮壽陽，為南譙太守，與叔業有隙，單騎奔魏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiahou Daoyi of Qiao, as General Who Assists the State, followed Pei Shuye in garrisoning Shouyang and served as Administrator of Southern Qiao. He had a rift with Shuye and fled alone on horseback to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiahou Daoyi of Qiao, serving as General Who Assists the State under Pei Shuye at Shouyang as Administrator of Southern Qiao, had a falling-out with Shuye and fled alone on horseback to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以道遷為驍騎將軍，從王肅鎮壽陽，使道遷守合肥。

translations.literal: Wei made Daoyi General of Valiant Cavalry; he followed Wang Su in garrisoning Shouyang, and Wei had Daoyi defend Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Daoyi General of Valiant Cavalry. He followed Wang Su in garrisoning Shouyang, and Wei had Daoyi defend Hefei.

sentences.zh: 肅卒，道遷棄戍來奔，從梁、秦二州刺史莊丘黑鎮南鄭；

translations.literal: When Su died, Daoyi abandoned his post and came over to Liang, following Zhuangqiu Hei, Governor of Liang and Qin provinces, in garrisoning Nanzheng;
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, Daoyi abandoned his post and defected to Liang, serving under Zhuangqiu Hei, Governor of Liang and Qin provinces, at Nanzheng;

sentences.zh: 以道遷為長史，領漢中太守。

translations.literal: Daoyi was made Chief Clerk and concurrently Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi was appointed Chief Clerk and concurrently Administrator of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 黑卒，詔以都官尚書王珍國為刺史，未至，道遷陰與軍主考城江忱之等謀降魏。

translations.literal: When Hei died, an edict appointed Wang Zhenguo, Minister of Justice, as Governor; before he arrived, Daoyi secretly plotted with Army Commander Jiang Chenzhi of Kaocheng and others to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Hei died, the court appointed Wang Zhenguo, Minister of Justice, as governor, but before he arrived Daoyi secretly plotted with Army Commander Jiang Chenzhi of Kaocheng and others to surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏仇池鎮將楊靈珍叛魏來奔，朝延以為征虜將軍、假武都王，助戍漢中，有部曲六百餘人，道遷憚之。

translations.literal: Before this, Yang Lingzhen, garrison commander of Chouchi in Wei, rebelled against Wei and came over; the court made him General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Acting King of Wudu, to assist in garrisoning Hanzhong, with more than six hundred retainers. Daoyi feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Lingzhen, the Wei garrison commander of Chouchi, had rebelled against Wei and defected. The court appointed him General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Acting King of Wudu to help garrison Hanzhong, with more than six hundred retainers. Daoyi feared him.

sentences.zh: 上遣左右吳公之等使南鄭。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched attendants Wu Gongzhi and others to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched his attendants Wu Gongzhi and others to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 道遷遂殺使者，發兵擊靈珍父子、斬之，並使者首送於魏。

translations.literal: Daoyi then killed the envoys, raised troops, attacked and beheaded Lingzhen and his son, and sent their heads together with the envoys' heads to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi then killed the envoys, raised troops, attacked and beheaded Lingzhen and his son, and sent their heads together with the envoys' heads to Wei.

sentences.zh: 白馬戍主君天寶聞之，引兵擊道遷，敗其將龐樹，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: Jun Tianbao, commander of the Baima garrison, heard of this and led troops to attack Daoyi, defeated his general Pang Shu, and then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Tianbao, commander of the Baima garrison, heard of this and led troops against Daoyi, defeated his general Pang Shu, and then besieged Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 道遷求救於氐王楊紹先、楊集起、楊集義，皆不應，集義弟集郎獨引兵救道遷，擊天寶，殺之。

translations.literal: Daoyi sought aid from the Di kings Yang Shaoxian, Yang Jiji, and Yang Jiyi; none responded. Jiyi's younger brother Jilang alone led troops to rescue Daoyi, attacked Tianbao, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi sought aid from the Di kings Yang Shaoxian, Yang Jiji, and Yang Jiyi, but none responded. Only Jiyi's younger brother Jilang led troops to rescue Daoyi, attacked Tianbao, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 魏以道遷為平南將軍、豫州刺史、豐縣侯。

translations.literal: Wei made Daoyi General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Marquis of Feng County.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Daoyi General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Marquis of Feng County.

sentences.zh: 又以尚書刑巒為鎮西將軍、都督征梁、漢諸軍事，將兵赴之。

translations.literal: Xing Luan of the Secretariat was also made General Who Guards the West and Supervisor of all military affairs for campaigns against Liang and Han, and led troops to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also appointed Xing Luan of the Secretariat General Who Guards the West and Supervisor of all military affairs for campaigns against Liang and Han, and sent him with troops to the region.

sentences.zh: 道遷受平南，辭豫州，且求公爵，魏主不許。

translations.literal: Daoyi accepted Pacifies the South but declined Yuzhou and also requested a ducal title; the Wei sovereign did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi accepted the post of Pacifies the South but declined Yuzhou and also asked for a ducal title; the Wei emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinhai the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏以驃騎大將軍高陽王雍為司空，加尚書令廣陽王嘉儀同三司。

translations.literal: On yichou Wei made the General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Gaoyang, Minister of Works, and added to Minister of the Secretariat Guangyang Wang Jia the privilege of Three Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Wei appointed the General of Agile Cavalry, the Prince of Gaoyang, Minister of Works, and granted Minister of the Secretariat Guangyang Wang Jia the privilege of Three Insignia.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，魏以宕昌世子梁彌博為宕昌王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi Wei made Liang Mibo, heir of Dangchang, King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingzi Wei made Liang Mibo, heir of Dangchang, King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 上謀伐魏，壬午，遣衛尉卿楊公則將宿衛兵塞洛口。

translations.literal: The emperor planned to attack Wei; on renwu he dispatched Yang Gongze, Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan, to lead the palace guard and block Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to attack Wei. On renwu he dispatched Yang Gongze, Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan, to lead the palace guard and block Luokou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，交州刺史李凱據州反，長史李畟討平之。

translations.literal: On renchen Li Kai, Inspector of Jiaozhou, seized the province in rebellion; Chief Clerk Li Yi suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Li Kai, Inspector of Jiaozhou, seized the province in rebellion; Chief Clerk Li Yi put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 魏邢巒至漢中，擊諸城戍，所向摧破。

translations.literal: Xing Luan of Wei reached Hanzhong and attacked the various walled posts; wherever he went he smashed through.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan of Wei reached Hanzhong and attacked the various garrison towns; wherever he went he carried all before him.

sentences.zh: 晉壽太守王景胤據石亭，巒遣統軍李義珍擊走之。

translations.literal: Wang Jingyin, Administrator of Jinshou, held Shiting; Luan dispatched Commander Li Yizhen, who attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingyin, Administrator of Jinshou, held Shiting; Luan sent Commander Li Yizhen, who attacked and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 魏以巒為梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei made Luan Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Luan Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 巴西太守龐景民據郡不下，郡民嚴玄思聚眾自稱巴州刺史，附於魏，攻景民，斬之。

translations.literal: Pang Jingmin, Administrator of Baxi, held the commandery and would not submit; a commandery man, Yan Xuan'en, gathered a crowd, styled himself Inspector of Bazhou, attached himself to Wei, attacked Jingmin, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jingmin, Administrator of Baxi, held the commandery and refused to submit. A local man, Yan Xuan'en, gathered a force, styled himself Inspector of Bazhou, submitted to Wei, attacked Jingmin, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 楊集起、集義聞魏克漢中而懼，閏月，帥群氐叛魏，斷漢中糧道，巒屢遣軍擊破之。

translations.literal: Yang Jiji and Jiyi, hearing that Wei had taken Hanzhong, were afraid; in the intercalary month they led the Di tribes in rebellion against Wei, cut Hanzhong's grain route, and Luan repeatedly sent troops that defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiji and Jiyi, hearing that Wei had taken Hanzhong, were alarmed. In the intercalary month they led the Di tribes in revolt against Wei and cut Hanzhong's supply lines; Luan repeatedly sent troops and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁巳，以行宕昌王梁彌博為河、涼二州刺史、宕昌王。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi the Acting King of Dangchang, Liang Mibo, was made Governor of He and Liang provinces and King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingsi the Acting King of Dangchang, Liang Mibo, was appointed Governor of He and Liang provinces and King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍孔陵等將兵二萬戍深杭，魯方達戍南安，任僧褒等戍石同，以拒魏。

translations.literal: Champion General Kong Ling and others led twenty thousand troops to garrison Shenhang; Lu Fangda garrisoned Nan'an; Ren Sengbao and others garrisoned Shitong, to resist Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Kong Ling and others led twenty thousand troops to garrison Shenhang; Lu Fangda garrisoned Nan'an; Ren Sengbao and others garrisoned Shitong to resist Wei.

sentences.zh: 刑巒遣統軍王足將兵擊之，所至皆捷，遂入劍閣。

translations.literal: Xing Luan dispatched Commander Wang Zu to lead troops against them; wherever he went he was victorious and then entered Jiange Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan sent Commander Wang Zu with troops against them; wherever he went he was victorious, and he then entered Jiange Pass.

sentences.zh: 陵等退保梓潼，足又進擊破之。

translations.literal: Ling and the others retreated to defend Zitong; Zu advanced again and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ling and the others fell back to defend Zitong; Zu advanced again and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 梁州十四郡地，東西七百里，南北千里，皆入於魏。

translations.literal: The territory of Liang province's fourteen commanderies—seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south—all came under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The territory of Liang province's fourteen commanderies—seven hundred li east to west and a thousand li north to south—all fell to Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，益州刺史當陽侯鄧元起以母老乞歸，詔征為右衛將軍，以西昌侯淵藻代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Deng Yuanqi, Marquis of Dangyang and Inspector of Yizhou, begged to return because his mother was old; an edict summoned him as General of the Right Guard, and Xiao Yuanzao, Marquis of Xichang, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Deng Yuanqi, Marquis of Dangyang and Inspector of Yizhou, asked to return home because his mother was old. The court summoned him to serve as General of the Right Guard and replaced him with Xiao Yuanzao, Marquis of Xichang.

sentences.zh: 淵藻，懿之子也。

translations.literal: Yuanzao was the son of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao was the son of Xiao Yi.

sentences.zh: 夏侯道遷之叛也，尹天寶馳使報元起。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Daoyi rebelled, Yin Tianbao sent a fast courier to report to Yuanqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Daoyi rebelled, Yin Tianbao sent a fast courier to report to Yuanqi.

sentences.zh: 及魏寇晉壽，王景胤等並遣告急，眾勸元起急救之，元起曰：「朝廷萬里，軍不猝至，若寇賊侵淫，方須撲討，董督之任，非我而誰，何事匆匆救之！」

translations.literal: When Wei raided Jinshou, Wang Jingyin and others all sent urgent appeals; the crowd urged Yuanqi to rescue them at once. Yuanqi said: "The court is ten thousand li away; troops cannot arrive suddenly. If bandits spread their ravages, then suppression will be needed. The duty of overall command—if not me, then who? Why rush to rescue them!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wei raided Jinshou, Wang Jingyin and others all sent urgent appeals for help. Many urged Yuanqi to rescue them at once. Yuanqi said: "The court is ten thousand li away; troops cannot arrive overnight. If the enemy spreads unchecked, someone must take charge of the suppression—and if not I, then who? Why rush off to rescue them!"

sentences.zh: 詔假元起都督征討諸軍事，救漢中，而晉壽已陷。

translations.literal: An edict provisionally made Yuanqi Supervisor of all military affairs for punitive campaigns and ordered him to rescue Hanzhong, but Jinshou had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict provisionally appointed Yuanqi Supervisor of all military affairs for punitive campaigns and ordered him to rescue Hanzhong, but Jinshou had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 蕭淵藻將至，元起營還裝，糧儲器械，取之無遺。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yuanzao was about to arrive, Yuanqi packed up his camp for the return journey; grain stores and weapons—he took them all without leaving anything.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yuanzao was about to arrive, Yuanqi packed up his camp for departure and took every scrap of grain stores and weapons, leaving nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 淵藻入城，恨之；

translations.literal: Yuanzao entered the city and resented this;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao entered the city and resented this;

sentences.zh: 又救其良馬，元起曰：「年少郎子，何用馬為！」

translations.literal: He also asked for Yuanqi's fine horses. Yuanqi said: "Young fellow, what do you need horses for!"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for Yuanqi's fine horses. Yuanqi said: "Young fellow, what do you need horses for!"

sentences.zh: 淵藻恚，因醉，殺之，元起麾下圍城，哭，且問故，淵藻曰：「天子有詔。」

translations.literal: Yuanzao was furious; while drunk he killed him. Yuanqi's subordinates surrounded the city, weeping, and asked the reason. Yuanzao said: "The Son of Heaven had an edict."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao was furious; while drunk he killed him. Yuanqi's subordinates surrounded the city, weeping, and demanded an explanation. Yuanzao said: "The Son of Heaven had issued an edict."

sentences.zh: 眾乃散。

translations.literal: The crowd then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The men then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 遂誣以反，上疑焉。

translations.literal: He then slandered Yuanqi as a rebel; the emperor was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: He then accused Yuanqi of rebellion, and the emperor was suspicious.

sentences.zh: 元起故吏廣漢羅研詣闕訟之，上曰：「果如我所量也！」

translations.literal: Yuanqi's former clerk Luo Yan of Guanghan went to the capital to bring suit; the emperor said: "It is indeed as I reckoned!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi's former clerk Luo Yan of Guanghan went to the capital to bring suit. The emperor said: "It is exactly as I suspected!"

sentences.zh: 使讓淵藻曰：「元起為汝報仇，汝為仇報仇，忠孝之道如何！」

translations.literal: He sent someone to reprove Yuanzao: "Yuanqi avenged you—yet you avenged yourself upon your avenger. What of the way of loyalty and filial piety!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to reprove Yuanzao: "Yuanqi avenged your family—yet you took revenge on the man who avenged you. What becomes of loyalty and filial piety!"

sentences.zh: 乃貶淵藻號為冠軍將軍；

translations.literal: Yuanzao's title was then reduced to Champion General;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao's title was then reduced to Champion General;

sentences.zh: 贈元起征西將軍，謚曰忠侯。

translations.literal: Yuanqi was posthumously given General Who Conquers the West, with the posthumous title Marquis of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi was posthumously given the title General Who Conquers the West, with the posthumous name Loyal Marquis.

sentences.zh: 李延壽論曰：元起勤乃胥附，功惟闢土，勞之不圖，禍機先陷。

translations.literal: Li Yanshou commented: Yuanqi's diligence lay in winning adherents; his merit lay only in opening territory. His labors were unrewarded, and the engine of disaster trapped him first.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshou commented: Yuanqi's diligence lay in winning followers; his merit lay in opening new territory. His labors went unrewarded, and the seeds of disaster caught him first.

sentences.zh: 冠軍之貶，於罰已輕。

translations.literal: The Champion's demotion was already light as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The demotion of the Champion General was already a light punishment.

sentences.zh: 梁之政刑，於斯為失。

translations.literal: In Liang's governance and punishments, here was failure.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's governance and punishments, here was a grave failure.

sentences.zh: 私戚之端，自斯而啟。

translations.literal: The beginning of private kin favoritism opened from this.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of favoring private kin began from this point.

sentences.zh: 年之不永，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: That his years were not long—is this not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: That his reign was not long—is this not only to be expected!

sentences.zh: 益州民焦僧護聚眾數萬作亂，蕭淵藻年未弱冠，集僚佐議自擊之；

translations.literal: Jiao Seng'hu of Yizhou gathered a crowd of tens of thousands in rebellion. Xiao Yuanzao was not yet twenty; he assembled his staff to discuss attacking them himself;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Seng'hu of Yizhou gathered tens of thousands in rebellion. Xiao Yuanzao was not yet twenty; he assembled his staff to discuss leading the attack himself;

sentences.zh: 或陳不可，淵藻大怒，斬於階側。

translations.literal: some stated it could not be done; Yuanzao was greatly angered and beheaded them beside the steps.
translations.idiomatic: some objected that it could not be done; Yuanzao flew into a rage and beheaded them beside the steps.

sentences.zh: 乃乘平肩輿巡行賊壘。

translations.literal: He then rode a level-shouldered litter and toured the rebel camps.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode in an open litter and toured the rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 賊弓亂射，矢下如雨，從者舉楯御矢，淵藻命去之。

translations.literal: The rebels shot bows wildly; arrows fell like rain. Attendants raised shields to ward off the arrows; Yuanzao ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shot wildly; arrows fell like rain. His attendants raised shields to ward off the arrows, but Yuanzao ordered them taken away.

sentences.zh: 由是人心大安，擊僧護等，皆平之。

translations.literal: Thereby the people's hearts were greatly reassured; he attacked Seng'hu and the others and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the people's hearts were greatly reassured. He attacked Seng'hu and the others and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚戌，初立孔子廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengxu, the Temple of Confucius was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengxu, the Temple of Confucius was established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史王超宗將兵圍魏小峴。

translations.literal: Wang Chaozong, Inspector of Yuzhou, led troops to besiege Wei's Little Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chaozong, Inspector of Yuzhou, led troops to besiege Wei's Little Xian.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏揚州刺史薛真度遣兼統軍李叔仁等擊之，超宗兵大敗。

translations.literal: On dingmao Xue Zhendu, Inspector of Yangzhou in Wei, dispatched Acting Commander Li Shuren and others to attack them; Chaozong's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Xue Zhendu, Wei's Inspector of Yangzhou, dispatched Acting Commander Li Shuren and others to attack them; Chaozong's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍王景胤、李畎、輔國將軍魯方達等與魏王足戰，屢敗。

translations.literal: Champion General Wang Jingyin, Li Qu, and General Who Assists the State Lu Fangda and others fought Wang Zu of Wei and were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Wang Jingyin, Li Qu, General Who Assists the State Lu Fangda, and others fought Wang Zu of Wei and were repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，足進逼涪城。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zu advanced and pressed Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zu advanced and pressed Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，魏中山王英寇雍州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei invaded Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei invaded Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，秦、梁二州刺史魯方達與魏王足統軍紀洪雅、盧祖遷戰，敗，方達等十五將皆死。

translations.literal: On gengxu Lu Fangda, Governor of Qin and Liang provinces, fought with Wang Zu of Wei's commanders Ji Hongya and Lu Zuqian and was defeated; Fangda and fifteen other generals all died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Lu Fangda, Governor of Qin and Liang provinces, fought Wang Zu's commanders Ji Hongya and Lu Zuqian and was defeated; Fangda and fifteen other generals were killed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，王景胤等又與祖遷城，敗，景胤等二十四將皆死。

translations.literal: On renzi Wang Jingyin and others again fought Zuqian at the city and were defeated; Jingyin and twenty-four other generals all died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Wang Jingyin and others fought Zuqian again and were defeated; Jingyin and twenty-four other generals were killed.

sentences.zh: 楊公則至洛口，與魏豫州長史石榮戰，斬之。

translations.literal: Yang Gongze reached Luokou, fought with Shi Rong, Chief Clerk of Yuzhou in Wei, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze reached Luokou, fought Shi Rong, Chief Clerk of Yuzhou in Wei, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，將軍姜慶真與魏戰於羊石，不利，公則退屯馬頭。

translations.literal: On jiayin General Jiang Qingzhen fought Wei at Yangshi with an unfavorable outcome; Gongze withdrew and encamped at Matou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin General Jiang Qingzhen fought Wei at Yangshi with an unfavorable outcome; Gongze withdrew and encamped at Matou.

sentences.zh: 雍州蠻沔東太守田青喜叛降魏。

translations.literal: Tian Qingxi, Administrator of Mian East among the Yongzhou barbarians, rebelled and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qingxi, Administrator of Mian East among the Yongzhou tribes, rebelled and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏有芝生於太極殿之西序，魏主以示侍中崔光。

translations.literal: In Wei a fungus grew in the western wing of the Hall of Supreme Pole; the Wei sovereign showed it to Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei a fungus grew in the western wing of the Hall of Supreme Pole; the Wei emperor showed it to Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang.

sentences.zh: 光上表，以為：「此《莊子》所謂『氣蒸成菌』者也。

translations.literal: Guang submitted a memorial, stating: "This is what Zhuangzi called 'vapor steaming into fungus.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted a memorial, stating: "This is what Zhuangzi called 'vapor steaming into fungus.

sentences.zh: 柔脆之物，生於墟落穢溫之地，不當生於殿堂高華之處；

translations.literal: A soft, fragile thing grows in ruined hamlets and foul, warm places; it ought not grow in lofty, splendid halls;
translations.idiomatic: A soft, fragile thing grows in ruined hamlets and foul, warm places; it ought not grow in lofty, splendid halls;

sentences.zh: 今忽有之，厥狀扶疏，誠足異也。

translations.literal: now it has suddenly appeared here, its form luxuriant—truly strange enough.
translations.idiomatic: yet now it has suddenly appeared here, its form luxuriant—truly strange indeed.

sentences.zh: 夫野木生朝，野鳥入廟，古人皆以為敗亡之象，故太戊、中宗懼災修德，殷道以昌，所謂『家利而怪先，國興而妖豫』者也。

translations.literal: When wild trees grow in the court and wild birds enter the temple, the ancients all took these as omens of ruin; therefore Taojia and Zhongzong feared calamity and cultivated virtue, and the Yin way flourished—what is called 'when the house is about to prosper, monsters come first; when the state is about to rise, portents appear beforehand.'
translations.idiomatic: When wild trees grow in the court and wild birds enter the temple, the ancients all took these as omens of ruin; therefore Taojia and Zhongzong feared calamity and cultivated virtue, and the Yin dynasty flourished—what is meant by 'when the house is about to prosper, monsters appear first; when the state is about to rise, portents come beforehand.'

sentences.zh: 今西南二方，兵革未息，郊甸之內，大旱逾時，民勞物悴，菲此之甚，承天育民者所宜矜恤。

translations.literal: Now in the southwest and west war has not ceased; within the capital suburbs great drought has lasted beyond its season; the people are weary and things are exhausted—nothing exceeds this in wretchedness. Those who receive Heaven's mandate and nurture the people ought to show compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Now war has not ceased in the southwest and west; within the capital suburbs a great drought has lasted beyond its season; the people are weary and resources exhausted—nothing exceeds this in misery. Those who receive Heaven's mandate and nurture the people ought to show compassion.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下側躬聳意，惟新聖道，節夜飲之樂，養方富之年，則魏祚可以永隆，皇壽等於山嶽矣。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty would bend your person and lift your mind, renew the sage Way, moderate the pleasures of nightly drinking, and nurture the years when the realm is just growing rich—then Wei's fortune may endure forever and Your Majesty's years equal mountains."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish Your Majesty would humble yourself and renew your mind, refresh the sage Way, moderate the pleasures of nightly feasting, and nurture the years when the realm is just growing prosperous—then Wei's fortune may endure forever and Your Majesty's years may equal the mountains."

sentences.zh: 於是魏主好宴樂，故光言及之。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign was fond of feasting and music; therefore Guang spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was fond of feasting and music; therefore Guang spoke of this.

sentences.zh: 九月，己巳，楊公則等與魏揚州刺史元嵩戰，公則敗績。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jisi, Yang Gongze and others fought Yuan Song, Inspector of Yangzhou in Wei; Gongze was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jisi, Yang Gongze and others fought Yuan Song, Wei's Inspector of Yangzhou; Gongze was defeated.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，上大舉伐魏，以揚州刺史臨川王宏都督北討諸軍事，尚書右僕射柳惔為副，王公以下各上國租及田谷以助軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu the emperor launched a major campaign against Wei, making the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, Inspector of Yangzhou, Supervisor of all northern expedition military affairs, with Liu Yan, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, as deputy; princes, dukes, and below each submitted state rents and field grain to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu the emperor launched a major campaign against Wei. He appointed the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, Inspector of Yangzhou, Supervisor of all northern expedition military affairs, with Liu Yan, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, as deputy. Princes, dukes, and officials below each submitted state rents and field grain to support the army.

sentences.zh: 宏軍於洛口。

translations.literal: Hong encamped at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong encamped at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 楊集起、集義立楊紹先為帝，自皆稱王。

translations.literal: Yang Jiji and Jiyi set up Yang Shaoxian as emperor; they themselves all styled themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiji and Jiyi set up Yang Shaoxian as emperor; they themselves all took royal titles.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊辰朔，魏遣光祿大夫楊椿將兵討之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuchen the new moon, Wei dispatched Yang Chun, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuchen the new moon, Wei dispatched Yang Chun, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 魏王足圍涪城，蜀人震恐，益州城戍降魏者什二三，民自上名籍者五萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Wang Zu of Wei besieged Fucheng; the people of Shu were shaken with fear. Of Yizhou's walled garrisons, two or three tenths surrendered to Wei; commoners who submitted their own household registers numbered more than fifty thousand families.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zu of Wei besieged Fucheng; the people of Shu were shaken with fear. Two or three tenths of Yizhou's garrison towns surrendered to Wei, and more than fifty thousand households voluntarily registered their names.

sentences.zh: 刑巒表於魏主，請乘勝取蜀，以為：「建康、成都，相去萬里，陸行既絕，惟資水路。

translations.literal: Xing Luan memorialized the Wei sovereign, asking to take advantage of victory to seize Shu, stating: "Jiankang and Chengdu are ten thousand li apart; overland travel is already cut off, and only the water route remains.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan memorialized the Wei emperor, urging that they seize the moment to take Shu. He argued: "Jiankang and Chengdu are ten thousand li apart; overland routes are already cut off, and only the water route remains.

sentences.zh: 水軍西上，非同年不達，益州外無軍援，一可圖也。

translations.literal: A fleet going west cannot arrive within the same year; outside Yizhou there is no military aid—first, it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: A fleet sailing west cannot arrive within a single year, and Yizhou has no military aid from outside—first, it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 頃經劉季連反，鄧元起攻圍，資儲空竭，吏民無復固守之志，二可圖也。

translations.literal: Recently there was Liu Jilian's rebellion and Deng Yuanqi's siege; stores are emptied and officials and people no longer have the will to hold firm—second, it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Liu Jilian rebelled and Deng Yuanqi besieged the province; stores are exhausted and officials and people no longer have the will to hold firm—second, it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 蕭淵藻裙屐少年，未洽治務，宿昔名將，多見囚戮，今之所任，皆左右少年，三可圖也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuanzao is a slipper-wearing youth who has not mastered governance; famous generals of old have mostly been imprisoned or killed; those now appointed are all young favorites at his side—third, it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuanzao is a pampered youth who has not mastered governance; famous generals of old have mostly been imprisoned or killed; those now in office are all young favorites at his side—third, it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 蜀之所恃，唯在劍閣，今既克南安，已奪其險，據彼竟內，三分已一；

translations.literal: What Shu relies on is only Jiange Pass; now that Nan'an has been taken, its peril has already been seized, and one-third of that territory within its borders is held;
translations.idiomatic: Shu relies only on Jiange Pass; now that Nan'an has been taken, its strategic barrier is lost, and one-third of its territory within the borders is already held;

sentences.zh: 自南安向涪，方軌無礙，前軍累敗，後眾喪魄，四可圖也。

translations.literal: from Nan'an toward Fu the road is unobstructed on equal wheel-tracks; the forward armies have been repeatedly defeated and the rear masses have lost their spirits—fourth, it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: from Nan'an toward Fu the road lies open; the forward armies have been repeatedly defeated and the rear forces have lost heart—fourth, it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 淵藻是蕭衍骨肉至親，必無處理，若克涪城，淵藻安青城中坐而受困，必將望風逃去；

translations.literal: Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's closest kin by blood and surely cannot manage affairs; if Fucheng is taken, Yuanzao will sit in Qingcheng and accept encirclement—he is sure to flee at the first rumor of defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzao is Xiao Yan's closest kinsman and surely cannot manage affairs; if Fucheng is taken, Yuanzao will sit in Chengdu and accept encirclement—he is sure to flee at the first sign of defeat;

sentences.zh: 若其出鬥，庸、蜀士卒駑怯，弓矢寡弱，五可圖也。

translations.literal: if he comes out to fight, the soldiers of Yong and Shu are dull and timid, their bows and arrows few and weak—fifth, it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: if he comes out to fight, the soldiers of Yong and Shu are dull and timid, their bows and arrows few and weak—fifth, it can be taken.

sentences.zh: 臣內省文吏，不習軍旅，賴將士竭力，頻有薄捷。

translations.literal: I, inwardly examining myself, am a civil clerk who does not practice military affairs; relying on the generals' and soldiers' full effort, we have had frequent slight victories.
translations.idiomatic: I am by nature a civil official untrained in military affairs; relying on the generals' and soldiers' full effort, we have had frequent minor victories.

sentences.zh: 既克重阻，民心懷服，瞻望涪、益，旦夕可屠。

translations.literal: Having already taken the heavy barriers, the people's hearts are won over; gazing toward Fu and Yi, they can be slaughtered within days.
translations.idiomatic: Having already taken the major barriers, the people's hearts are won over; looking toward Fu and Yi, they can be taken within days.

sentences.zh: 正以兵少糧匱，未宜前出，今若不取，後圖便難。

translations.literal: It is just that with few troops and scant grain it is not yet fitting to advance; if we do not take it now, later plans will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that with few troops and scant grain it is not yet fitting to advance; if we do not take Shu now, later plans will be far more difficult.

sentences.zh: 況益州殷實。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yizhou is rich and substantial.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yizhou is rich and substantial.

sentences.zh: 戶口十萬，比壽春、義陽，其利三倍。

translations.literal: Its registered households number a hundred thousand; compared with Shouchun and Yiyang, its profit is threefold.
translations.idiomatic: It has a hundred thousand registered households; compared with Shouchun and Yiyang, its profit is three times as great.

sentences.zh: 朝廷若欲進取，時不可失；

translations.literal: If the court wishes to advance and seize it, the time must not be lost;
translations.idiomatic: If the court wishes to advance and seize it, the moment must not be lost;

sentences.zh: 若欲保境寧民，則臣居此無事，乞歸侍養。」

translations.literal: if it wishes only to secure the borders and give the people peace, then I have nothing to do here and beg to return and attend my parents."
translations.idiomatic: if it wishes only to secure the borders and give the people peace, then I have nothing to do here and beg to return home to care for my parents."

sentences.zh: 魏主詔以「平蜀之舉，當更聽後敕。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign issued an edict stating: "The campaign to pacify Shu shall await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor issued an edict stating: "The campaign to pacify Shu shall await further orders.

sentences.zh: 寇難未夷，何得以養親為辭！」

translations.literal: Bandit troubles are not yet pacified—how can you use caring for your parents as an excuse!"
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is not yet pacified—how can you use caring for your parents as an excuse!"

sentences.zh: 巒又表稱：「昔鄧艾、鐘會帥十八萬眾，傾中國資儲，僅能平蜀，所以然者，斗實力也。

translations.literal: Luan memorialized again, stating: "In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led a hundred and eighty thousand men and exhausted the Central Kingdom's stores, barely able to pacify Shu—the reason was that they matched strength for strength.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again, stating: "In the past Deng Ai and Zhong Hui led a hundred and eighty thousand men and exhausted the empire's stores, barely able to pacify Shu—the reason was that they matched strength for strength.

sentences.zh: 況臣才非古人，何宜以二萬之眾而希平蜀！

translations.literal: Moreover, my talent is not that of the ancients—how is it fitting to hope to pacify Shu with only twenty thousand men!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my talent falls far short of the ancients—how can I hope to pacify Shu with only twenty thousand men!

sentences.zh: 所以敢者，正以據得要險，士民慕義。

translations.literal: The reason I dare is precisely that we hold the vital passes and the gentry and people admire our righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I dare attempt it is precisely that we hold the vital passes and the gentry and people admire our cause.

sentences.zh: 此往則易，彼來則難，任力而行，理有可克。

translations.literal: Going thither is easy; coming hither is hard; acting according to strength, reason holds that it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Going west is easy; coming east is hard; acting according to our strength, it stands to reason that we can prevail.

sentences.zh: 今王足已逼涪城，脫得涪，則益州乃成擒之物，但得之有早晚耳。

translations.literal: Now Wang Zu has already pressed Fucheng; if Fu is taken, then Yizhou becomes something already in hand—only whether it is gained sooner or later.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Zu has already pressed Fucheng; if Fu is taken, Yizhou becomes something already in our grasp—only a question of sooner or later.

sentences.zh: 且梓潼已附民戶數萬，朝廷豈可不守！

translations.literal: Moreover, Zitong has already submitted with tens of thousands of households—how can the court fail to hold it!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zitong has already submitted with tens of thousands of households—how can the court fail to hold it!

sentences.zh: 又，劍閣天險，得而棄之，良可惜矣！

translations.literal: Again, Jiange Pass is a heaven-sent barrier—to gain it and then abandon it would be truly regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Again, Jiange Pass is a heaven-sent barrier—to gain it and then abandon it would be a grievous waste!

sentences.zh: 臣誠知戰伐危事，未易可為。

translations.literal: I truly know that warfare is a perilous affair and not easily undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: I truly know that warfare is perilous and not easily undertaken.

sentences.zh: 自軍度劍閣以來，鬢髮中白，日夜戰懼，何可為心！

translations.literal: Since the army crossed Jiange Pass, my temples have turned half white; day and night I tremble in battle—what heart can I have!
translations.idiomatic: Since the army crossed Jiange Pass, my temples have turned half white; day and night I tremble with fear of battle—what peace of mind can I have!

sentences.zh: 所以勉強者，既得此地而自退不守，恐負陛下之爵祿故也。

translations.literal: The reason I force myself on is that, having gained this territory, to withdraw and not hold it would mean failing Your Majesty's rank and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I force myself to continue is that, having gained this territory, to withdraw and not hold it would mean failing the trust of Your Majesty's rank and stipend.

sentences.zh: 且臣之意算，正欲先取部城，以漸而進。

translations.literal: Moreover, my plan is precisely to take Fucheng first and advance step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my plan is precisely to take Fucheng first and advance step by step.

sentences.zh: 若得涪城，則中分益州之地，斷水陸之沖。

translations.literal: If Fucheng is taken, then Yizhou's territory is cut in half and the water and land routes are severed.
translations.idiomatic: If Fucheng is taken, Yizhou's territory is cut in half and the water and land routes are severed.

sentences.zh: 彼外無援軍，孤城自守，何能復持久哉！

translations.literal: They will have no aid from outside; a lone city holding itself—how can it endure long!
translations.idiomatic: They will have no aid from outside; a lone city holding out—how can it endure!

sentences.zh: 臣今欲使軍軍相次，聲勢連接，先為萬全之計，然後圖功；

translations.literal: I now wish to have the armies follow one another in succession, their momentum linked, first making plans for complete safety and only then seeking achievement;
translations.idiomatic: I now wish to have the armies follow one another in succession, their momentum linked, first making plans for complete safety and only then seeking victory;

sentences.zh: 得之則大利，不得則自全。

translations.literal: if we gain it, great profit; if not, we preserve ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: if we gain it, great profit; if not, we preserve ourselves.

sentences.zh: 又，巴西、南鄭，相距千四百里，去州迢遰，恆多擾動。

translations.literal: Again, Baxi and Nanzheng are fourteen hundred li apart, far from the provincial capital, and disturbances are constant.
translations.idiomatic: Again, Baxi and Nanzheng are fourteen hundred li apart, far from the provincial capital, and disturbances are constant.

sentences.zh: 昔在南之日，以其統綰勢難，曾立巴州，鎮靜夷、獠，梁州藉利，因而表罷。

translations.literal: In the days when I was in the south, because control was difficult over such a distance, Bazhou was once established to pacify the Yi and Liao; Liang province benefited, and therefore a memorial was submitted to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the south, because control was difficult over such a distance, Bazhou was once established to pacify the Yi and Liao tribes; Liang province benefited, and therefore a memorial was submitted to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 彼土民望，嚴、蒲、何、楊，非唯一族，雖率居山谷，而豪右甚多，文學風流，亦為不少，但以去州既遠，不獲仕進。

translations.literal: The leading clans of that land—Yan, Pu, He, Yang—are not of a single family; though they mostly dwell in mountain valleys, there are many powerful houses, and men of letters and refinement are not few, yet because they are so far from the province they cannot advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: The leading clans of that land—Yan, Pu, He, Yang—are not of a single family; though they mostly dwell in mountain valleys, there are many powerful houses, and men of letters and refinement are not few, yet because they are so far from the provincial capital they cannot advance in office.

sentences.zh: 至於州綱，無由廁跡，是以郁怏，多生異圖。

translations.literal: As for the provincial establishment, they have no way to take part in it; therefore they are resentful and often hatch rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: As for the provincial establishment, they have no way to take part in it; therefore they are resentful and often hatch rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 比道遷建義之始，嚴玄思自號巴州刺史，克城以來，仍使行事。

translations.literal: Recently, at the beginning of Daoyi's uprising, Yan Xuan'en styled himself Inspector of Bazhou; since the city was taken, he has continued to act in that capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, at the beginning of Daoyi's uprising, Yan Xuan'en styled himself Inspector of Bazhou; since the city was taken, he has continued to act in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 巴西廣袤千里，戶餘四萬，若於彼立州，鎮攝華、獠，則大貼民情，從墊江已還，不勞征伐，自為國有。」

translations.literal: Baxi extends a thousand li with more than forty thousand households; if a province were established there to pacify the Chinese and the Liao, it would greatly suit the people's feelings; from Dianjiang back, without the labor of campaigns, it would become our territory."
translations.idiomatic: Baxi extends a thousand li with more than forty thousand households; if a province were established there to pacify the Chinese and tribal peoples, it would greatly suit local sentiment; from Dianjiang westward, without campaigns, it would become our territory."

sentences.zh: 魏主不從。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏主以王足行益州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wei sovereign had made Wang Zu Acting Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wei emperor had made Wang Zu Acting Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣天門太守張齊將兵救益州，未至，魏主更以梁州軍司泰山羊祉為益州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Zhang Qi, Administrator of Tianmen, to lead troops to rescue Yizhou; before he arrived, the Wei sovereign replaced him with Yang Zhi of Taishan, Army Supervisor of Liang province, as Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Zhang Qi, Administrator of Tianmen, to lead troops to rescue Yizhou; before he arrived, the Wei emperor replaced Wang Zu with Yang Zhi of Taishan, Army Supervisor of Liang province, as Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 王足聞之，不悅，輒引兵還，遂不能定蜀。

translations.literal: Wang Zu heard of this, was displeased, and forthwith led his troops back; thus he could not settle Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zu heard of this, was displeased, and forthwith led his troops back; thus he could not settle Shu.

sentences.zh: 久之，足自魏來奔。

translations.literal: After a long while, Zu came over from Wei to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, Zu defected from Wei to Liang.

sentences.zh: 刑巒在梁州，接豪右以禮，撫小民以惠，州人悅之。

translations.literal: Xing Luan was in Liang province; he received the powerful clans with courtesy and treated the common people with kindness, and the people of the province were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan was in Liang province; he received the powerful clans with courtesy and treated the common people with kindness, and the people of the province were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 巒之克巴西也，使軍主李仲遷守之。

translations.literal: When Luan took Baxi, he had Army Commander Li Zhongqian defend it.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan took Baxi, he had Army Commander Li Zhongqian defend it.

sentences.zh: 仲遷溺於酒色，費散兵儲，公事諮承，無能見者。

translations.literal: Zhongqian was drowned in wine and women, squandered military stores, and when public business was referred to him, no one could gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqian was drowned in wine and women, squandered military stores, and when public business was referred to him, no one could gain an audience.

sentences.zh: 巒忿之切齒，仲遷懼，謀叛，城人斬其首，以城來降。

translations.literal: Luan gnashed his teeth in anger; Zhongqian was afraid and plotted rebellion; the people of the city beheaded him and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Luan gnashed his teeth in anger; Zhongqian was afraid and plotted rebellion; the people of the city beheaded him and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，魏遣驃騎大將軍源懷討武興氐，刑巒等並受節度。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, Wei dispatched Yuan Huai, General of Agile Cavalry, to suppress the Di of Wuxing; Xing Luan and others all received his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, Wei dispatched Yuan Huai, General of Agile Cavalry, to suppress the Di of Wuxing; Xing Luan and others all served under his command.

sentences.zh: 司徒、尚書令謝朏以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Xie Tiao, Minister of Works and Director of the Secretariat, left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao, Minister of Works and Director of the Secretariat, left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大穰，米斛三十錢。

translations.literal: This year there was a great harvest; rice was thirty cash per hu.
translations.idiomatic: This year there was a great harvest; rice sold for thirty cash per hu.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝二天監五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, the Martial Sovereign, second scroll, fifth year of Tianjian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fifth year of Tianjian (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元五零六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, 506 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, AD 506)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁卯朔，魏於後生子昌，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingmao the new moon, the Wei empress gave birth to a son, Chang, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingmao the new moon, the Wei empress gave birth to a son, Chang, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 楊集義圍魏關城，刑巒使建武將軍傅豎眼討之，集義逆戰，豎眼擊破之。

translations.literal: Yang Jiyi besieged Wei's Guancheng; Xing Luan sent Fu Shuyan, General Who Establishes Martial Power, to suppress him. Jiyi met him in battle; Shuyan attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiyi besieged Wei's Guancheng; Xing Luan sent Fu Shuyan, General Who Establishes Martial Power, to suppress him. Jiyi met him in battle, and Shuyan routed him.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，壬申，克武興，執楊紹先，送洛陽。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit, on renshen he took Wuxing, seized Yang Shaoxian, and sent him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory in pursuit, on renshen he took Wuxing, seized Yang Shaoxian, and sent him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 楊集起、楊集義亡走。

translations.literal: Yang Jiji and Yang Jiyi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiji and Yang Jiyi fled.

sentences.zh: 遂滅其國，以為武興鎮，又改為東益州。

translations.literal: Their state was then destroyed; it was made the Wuxing garrison and later changed to Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Their state was then destroyed; it was made the Wuxing garrison and later renamed Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以前司徒謝朏為中書監、司徒。

translations.literal: On yihai the former Minister of Works Xie Tiao was made Supervisor of the Secretariat and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the former Minister of Works Xie Tiao was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史桓和擊魏南青州，不克。

translations.literal: Huan He, Inspector of Jizhou, attacked Wei's Southern Qingzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan He, Inspector of Jizhou, attacked Wei's Southern Qingzhou but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 魏秦州屠各王灋智聚眾二千，推秦州主簿呂苟兒為主，改元建明，置百官，攻逼州郡。

translations.literal: Wang Fazhi the Tuge of Qinzhou in Wei gathered two thousand men, set up Lü Gou'er, Chief Clerk of Qinzhou, as leader, changed the era name to Jianming, established the full bureaucracy, and attacked and pressed the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fazhi the Tuge of Qinzhou in Wei gathered two thousand men, set up Lü Gou'er, Chief Clerk of Qinzhou, as leader, changed the era name to Jianming, established a full bureaucracy, and attacked the provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 涇州民陳瞻亦聚眾稱王，改元聖明。

translations.literal: Chen Zhan of Jingzhou also gathered a crowd and styled himself king, changing the era name to Shengming.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhan of Jingzhou also gathered a force and styled himself king, changing the era name to Shengming.

sentences.zh: 己卯，楊集起兄弟相帥降魏。

translations.literal: On jimao the brothers Yang Jiji led one another in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the brothers Yang Jiji surrendered to Wei together.

sentences.zh: 甲申，封皇子綱為晉安王。

translations.literal: On jiashen the imperial son Gang was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the imperial son Gang was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，魏主詔王公以上直言忠諫。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingchen, the Wei sovereign ordered princes, dukes, and above to speak frankly with loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingchen, the Wei emperor ordered princes, dukes, and officials of rank to speak frankly with loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史陽固上表，以為：「當今之務，宜親宗室，勤庶政，貴農桑，賤工賈，絕談虛窮微之論，簡桑門無用之費，以救饑寒之苦。」

translations.literal: Yang Gu, Attending Secretary in the Secretariat for Imperial Documents, submitted a memorial, stating: "The task of the present age should be to draw close to the imperial clan, attend diligently to common administration, value agriculture and sericulture, hold craftsmen and merchants cheap, cut off discussions of empty subtleties, reduce the useless expenses of Buddhist monks, and relieve the suffering of hunger and cold."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gu, Attending Secretary in the Secretariat for Imperial Documents, submitted a memorial, stating: "The task of the present age should be to draw close to the imperial clan, attend diligently to common administration, value agriculture and sericulture, hold craftsmen and merchants in low esteem, cut off discussions of empty subtleties, reduce the useless expenses of Buddhist monks, and relieve the suffering of hunger and cold."

sentences.zh: 時魏主委任高肇，疏薄宗室，好桑門之法，不親政事，故固言及之。

translations.literal: At the time the Wei sovereign entrusted Gao Zhao, was cold toward the imperial clan, favored Buddhist law, and did not attend to government affairs; therefore Gu spoke of these matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Wei emperor entrusted Gao Zhao, was cold toward the imperial clan, favored Buddhist practices, and did not attend to government affairs; therefore Gu spoke of these matters.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏遣右衛將軍元麗都督諸軍討呂苟兒。

translations.literal: On wuwu Wei dispatched Yuan Li, General of the Right Guard, as Supervisor of all armies to suppress Lü Gou'er.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Wei dispatched Yuan Li, General of the Right Guard, as Supervisor of all armies to suppress Lü Gou'er.

sentences.zh: 麗，小新成之子也。

translations.literal: Li was the son of Xiaoxincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li was the son of Xiaoxincheng.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，徐州刺史歷陽昌義之與魏平南將軍陳伯之戰於梁城，義之敗績。

translations.literal: On yichou Chang Yizhi of Liyang, Inspector of Xuzhou, fought Chen Bozhi, General Who Pacifies the South in Wei, at Liangcheng; Yizhi was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Chang Yizhi of Liyang, Inspector of Xuzhou, fought Chen Bozhi, General Who Pacifies the South in Wei, at Liangcheng; Yizhi was defeated.

sentences.zh: 將軍蕭昺將兵擊魏徐州，圍淮陽。

translations.literal: General Xiao Bing led troops to attack Wei's Xuzhou and besieged Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: General Xiao Bing led troops to attack Wei's Xuzhou and besieged Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingyin the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingyin the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏荊州刺史趙怡、平南將軍奚康生救淮陽。

translations.literal: On jimao Zhao Yi, Inspector of Jingzhou in Wei, and Xi Kangsheng, General Who Pacifies the South, rescued Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Zhao Yi, Inspector of Jingzhou in Wei, and Xi Kangsheng, General Who Pacifies the South, rescued Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 魏咸陽王禧之子翼，遇赦，求葬其父。

translations.literal: Yi, son of the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, encountered an amnesty and begged to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, son of the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, encountered an amnesty and begged to bury his father.

sentences.zh: 屢泣請於魏主，魏主不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly wept and pleaded with the Wei sovereign; the Wei sovereign did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly wept and pleaded with the Wei emperor; the Wei emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 癸未，翼與其弟昌、曄來奔。

translations.literal: On guiwei Yi came over with his brothers Chang and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Yi defected with his brothers Chang and Ye.

sentences.zh: 上以翼為咸陽王，翼以曄嫡母李妃之子也，請以爵讓之，上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor made Yi Prince of Xianyang; Yi, because Ye was the son of the principal consort Lady Li, asked to yield the title to him; the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Yi Prince of Xianyang; Yi, because Ye was the son of the principal consort Lady Li, asked to yield the title to him; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍劉思效敗魏青州刺史元繫於膠水。

translations.literal: Liu Sixiao, General Who Assists the State, defeated Yuan Xi, Inspector of Qingzhou in Wei, at the Jiao River.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sixiao, General Who Assists the State, defeated Yuan Xi, Inspector of Qingzhou in Wei, at the Jiao River.

sentences.zh: 臨川王宏使記室吳興丘遲為書遺陳伯之曰：「尋君去就之際，非有它故，直以不能內審諸己，外受流言，沈迷猖蹶，以至於此。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linchuan, Hong, had his Recorder Qiu Chi of Wuxing write a letter and send it to Chen Bozhi, saying: "Reflecting on the moment of your going and staying, there was no other cause—you simply could not examine yourself within and outwardly accepted slanderous talk, sinking into delusion and reckless ruin, until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Linchuan, Hong, had his Recorder Qiu Chi of Wuxing write a letter to Chen Bozhi, saying: "Reflecting on the moment of your departure, there was no other cause—you simply could not examine yourself within and outwardly accepted slanderous talk, sinking into delusion and reckless ruin, until it came to this.

sentences.zh: 主上屈法申恩，吞舟是漏，將軍松柏不翦，親戚安居，高台未傾，愛妾尚在。

translations.literal: Our lord has bent the law to extend grace; even great offenders are spared. Your pines and cypresses have not been cut down, your kin dwell in peace, your high terrace has not fallen, and your beloved concubine is still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord has bent the law to extend grace; even great offenders are spared. Your ancestral groves have not been cut down, your kin dwell in peace, your high terrace has not fallen, and your beloved concubine is still alive.

sentences.zh: 而將軍魚游於沸鼎之中，燕巢于飛幕之上，不亦惑乎！

translations.literal: Yet you, General, swim like a fish in a boiling cauldron and nest like a swallow on a swaying curtain—is this not delusion!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you, General, swim like a fish in a boiling cauldron and nest like a swallow on a swaying curtain—is this not folly!

sentences.zh: 想早勵良圖，自求多福。」

translations.literal: I trust you will soon rouse yourself to a worthy plan and seek your own greater blessing."
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will soon rouse yourself to a worthy plan and secure your own greater blessing."

sentences.zh: 庚寅，伯之自壽陽梁城擁眾八千來降，魏人殺其子虎牙。

translations.literal: On gengyin Bozhi came over from Shouyang and Liangcheng at the head of eight thousand men; the Wei people killed his son Huya.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Bozhi defected from Shouyang and Liangcheng at the head of eight thousand men; the Wei people killed his son Huya.

sentences.zh: 詔復以伯之為西豫州刺史；

translations.literal: An edict restored Bozhi as Inspector of Western Yuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Bozhi as Inspector of Western Yuzhou;

sentences.zh: 未之任，復以為通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: before he took up the post, he was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: before he took up the post, he was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long while he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he died at home.

sentences.zh: 初，魏御史中尉甄琛表稱：「《周禮》，山林川澤有虞、衡之官，為之厲禁，蓋取之以時，不使戕賊而已，故雖置有司，實為民守之也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhen Chen, Imperial Inspecting Censor in Wei, memorialized, stating: "In the Rites of Zhou, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes had officials of Yu and Heng who set strict prohibitions—essentially taking from them according to season and not allowing wanton harm; therefore, though officials were established, in truth they guarded these things for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhen Chen, Imperial Inspecting Censor in Wei, memorialized, stating: "In the Rites of Zhou, mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes had officials of Yu and Heng who set strict prohibitions—essentially taking from them according to season and not allowing wanton harm; therefore, though officials were established, in truth they guarded these resources for the people.

sentences.zh: 夫一家之長，必惠養子孫，天下之君，必惠養兆民，未有為人父母而吝其醯醢，富有群生而榷其一物者也。

translations.literal: The head of a household must nourish his sons and grandsons with kindness; the ruler of all under Heaven must nourish the myriad people with kindness. Never has a parent been stingy with pickles and sauces, or a ruler possessed of all the living yet monopolized a single commodity.
translations.idiomatic: The head of a household must nourish his sons and grandsons with kindness; the ruler of all under Heaven must nourish the myriad people with kindness. Never has a parent been stingy with pickles and sauces, or a ruler possessed of all the living yet monopolized a single commodity.

sentences.zh: 今縣官鄣護河東鹽池而收其利，是專奉口腹而不及四體也。

translations.literal: Now the government protects the salt ponds of Hedong and collects their profit—this is to attend only the mouth and belly and neglect the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Now the government protects the salt ponds of Hedong and collects their profit—this is to attend only the mouth and belly and neglect the four limbs.

sentences.zh: 蓋天子富有四海，何患於貧！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven possesses the Four Seas—what worry has he of poverty!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven possesses the Four Seas—what worry has he of poverty!

sentences.zh: 乞弛鹽禁，與民共之。」

translations.literal: I beg that the salt prohibition be relaxed and shared with the people."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the salt prohibition be relaxed and shared with the people."

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事勰、尚書邢巒奏，以為：「琛之所陳，坐談則理高，行之則事闕。

translations.literal: Xie, Recorder of the Secretariat, and Xing Luan, Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, stating: "What Chen has presented is lofty in reason when discussed seated, but lacking in practice when carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, Recorder of the Secretariat, and Xing Luan, Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, stating: "What Chen has presented is lofty in theory when discussed at leisure, but impractical when carried out.

sentences.zh: 竊惟古之善治民者，必污隆隨時，豐儉稱事，役養消息以成其性命。

translations.literal: I reflect that those of old who governed the people well surely adapted to the times whether foul or fair, matched abundance or scarcity to affairs, and through labor, nurture, rest, and recovery completed their lives.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that those of old who governed the people well surely adapted to the times whether foul or fair, matched abundance or scarcity to affairs, and through labor, nurture, rest, and recovery sustained their lives.

sentences.zh: 若任其自生，隨其飲啄，乃是芻狗萬物，何以君為！

translations.literal: If one lets them live as they will and follow their eating and pecking, this is to treat all things as straw dogs—why have a ruler at all!
translations.idiomatic: If one lets them live as they will and follow their eating and pecking, this is to treat all things as straw dogs—why have a ruler at all!

sentences.zh: 是故聖人斂山澤之貨，以寬田疇之賦；

translations.literal: Therefore the sage gathers the goods of mountains and marshes to lighten the levies on fields;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage gathers the goods of mountains and marshes to lighten the levies on fields;

sentences.zh: 收關市之稅，以助什一之儲。

translations.literal: collects the taxes of passes and markets to aid the tithe stores.
translations.idiomatic: collects the taxes of passes and markets to aid the tithe stores.

sentences.zh: 取此與彼，皆非為身，所謂資天地之產，惠天地之民也。

translations.literal: Taking from this to give to that is none of it for oneself—what is called drawing on the produce of Heaven and Earth to benefit the people of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Taking from this to give to that is none of it for oneself—what is meant by drawing on the produce of Heaven and Earth to benefit the people of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 今鹽池之禁，為日已久，積而散之，以濟軍國，非專為供太官之膳羞，給後宮之服玩。

translations.literal: Now the prohibition on the salt ponds has been in force a long time; what is gathered and dispersed supports the army and state—it is not solely to supply the Grand Provisioner's delicacies or the rear palace's ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Now the prohibition on the salt ponds has been in force a long time; what is gathered and dispersed supports the army and state—it is not solely to supply the Grand Provisioner's delicacies or the rear palace's ornaments.

sentences.zh: 既利不在己，則彼我一也。

translations.literal: Since the profit is not in oneself, then theirs and ours are one.
translations.idiomatic: Since the profit does not go into one's own pocket, then theirs and ours are one.

sentences.zh: 然自禁鹽以來，有司多慢，出納之間，或不如法。

translations.literal: Yet since the salt prohibition, the officials have often been negligent; in receipts and disbursements they have sometimes not followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the salt prohibition, the officials have often been negligent; in receipts and disbursements they have sometimes not followed the law.

sentences.zh: 是使細民嗟怨，負販輕議，此乃用之者無方，非作之者有失也。

translations.literal: This makes the common people sigh in resentment and peddlers speak lightly in criticism—this is that those who apply it lack method, not that those who made it were at fault.
translations.idiomatic: This makes the common people sigh in resentment and peddlers speak lightly in criticism—this is that those who apply the policy lack method, not that those who made it were at fault.

sentences.zh: 一旦罷之，恐乖本旨。

translations.literal: To abolish it at once would, I fear, go against the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: To abolish it at once would, I fear, go against the original intent.

sentences.zh: 一行一改，法若弈棋，參論理要，宜如舊式。」

translations.literal: One act, one change—the law is like a game of chess; weighing the essentials of reason, it should remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: One act, one change—the law is like a game of chess; weighing the essentials of reason, it should remain as before."

sentences.zh: 魏主卒從琛議，夏，四月，乙未，罷鹽池禁。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign in the end followed Chen's proposal; in summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, the prohibition on the salt ponds was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor in the end followed Chen's proposal; in summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, the prohibition on the salt ponds was abolished.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，魏以中山王英為征南將軍、都督揚、徐二州諸軍事，帥眾十餘萬以拒梁軍，指授諸節度，所至以便宜從事。

translations.literal: On gengxu Wei made the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, General Who Campaigns South and Supervisor of all military affairs in Yang and Xu provinces, leading a host of more than a hundred thousand to resist the Liang army; he directed all commanders and wherever he went acted according to convenience.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Wei made the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, General Who Campaigns South and Supervisor of all military affairs in Yang and Xu provinces, leading more than a hundred thousand men to resist the Liang army; he directed all commanders and wherever he went acted at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史王茂將兵數萬侵魏荊州，誘魏邊民及諸蠻更立宛州，遣其所署宛州刺史雷豹狼等襲取魏河南城。

translations.literal: Wang Mao, Inspector of Jiangzhou, led tens of thousands of troops to invade Wei's Jingzhou, induced Wei's border people and various barbarians to re-establish Wanzhou, and dispatched his appointed Inspector of Wanzhou, Lei Baolang, and others to seize Wei's Henancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao, Inspector of Jiangzhou, led tens of thousands of troops to invade Wei's Jingzhou, induced Wei's border people and various tribes to re-establish Wanzhou, and dispatched his appointed Inspector of Wanzhou, Lei Baolang, and others to seize Wei's Henancheng.

sentences.zh: 魏遣平南將軍楊大眼都督諸軍擊茂，辛酉，茂戰敗，失亡二千餘人。

translations.literal: Wei dispatched Yang Dayan, General Who Pacifies the South, as Supervisor of all armies to attack Mao; on xinyou Mao was defeated and lost more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Wei dispatched Yang Dayan, General Who Pacifies the South, as Supervisor of all armies to attack Mao; on xinyou Mao was defeated and lost more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 大眼進攻河南城，茂逃還；

translations.literal: Dayan advanced to attack Henancheng; Mao fled back;
translations.idiomatic: Dayan advanced to attack Henancheng; Mao fled back;

sentences.zh: 大眼追至漢水，攻拔五城。

translations.literal: Dayan pursued to the Han River and took five cities.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan pursued to the Han River and took five cities.

sentences.zh: 魏徵虜將軍宇文福寇司州，俘千餘口而去。

translations.literal: Yuwen Fu, General Who Punishes the Barbarians in Wei, raided Sizhou, captured more than a thousand people, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Fu, General Who Punishes the Barbarians in Wei, raided Sizhou, captured more than a thousand people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛未，太子右衛率張惠紹等侵魏徐州，拔宿預，執城主馬成龍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on xinwei Zhang Huishao, Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and others invaded Wei's Xuzhou, took Suyu, and seized the city commander Ma Chenglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinwei Zhang Huishao, Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and others invaded Wei's Xuzhou, took Suyu, and seized the city commander Ma Chenglong.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，北徐州刺史昌義之拔梁城。

translations.literal: On yihai Chang Yizhi, Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, took Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Chang Yizhi, Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, took Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史韋睿遣長史王超等攻小峴，未拔。

translations.literal: Wei Rui, Inspector of Yuzhou, dispatched his Chief Clerk Wang Chao and others to attack Little Xian but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rui, Inspector of Yuzhou, dispatched his Chief Clerk Wang Chao and others to attack Little Xian but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 睿行圍柵，魏出數百人陳於門外，睿欲擊之，諸將皆曰：「向者輕來，未有戰備，徐還授甲，乃可進耳。」

translations.literal: Rui was building siege palisades when Wei sent out several hundred men to form ranks outside the gate. Rui wished to attack them; the generals all said: "We came lightly before and have no battle preparations; slowly return and don armor, then we can advance."
translations.idiomatic: Rui was building siege palisades when Wei sent out several hundred men to form ranks outside the gate. Rui wished to attack them; the generals all said: "We came lightly and have no battle preparations; let us return slowly, don armor, and then advance."

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Rui said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 魏城中二千餘人，足以固守，今無故出人於外，必其驍勇者也。

translations.literal: In the Wei city are more than two thousand men, enough to hold firm; now they come out without cause—these must be their fiercest fighters.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei garrison has more than two thousand men, enough to hold the city; now they come out without cause—these must be their fiercest fighters.

sentences.zh: 苟能挫之，其城自拔。」

translations.literal: If we can break them, the city will take itself."
translations.idiomatic: If we can break them, the city will fall of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 眾猶遲疑，睿指其節曰：』朝廷授此，非以為飾，韋睿法不可犯也！」

translations.literal: The crowd still hesitated; Rui pointed to his staff of office and said: "The court granted this not as ornament—Wei Rui's law cannot be violated!"
translations.idiomatic: The others still hesitated; Rui pointed to his staff of office and said: "The court granted this not as ornament—Wei Rui's law cannot be violated!"

sentences.zh: 遂進擊之，士皆殊死戰，魏兵敗走，因急攻之，中宿而拔，遂至合肥。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack; the soldiers all fought to the death; the Wei troops were defeated and fled; he pressed the attack urgently and took the city in the middle of the night, then proceeded to Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced to attack; his soldiers fought to the death; the Wei troops were routed; he pressed the attack urgently and took the city by midnight, then proceeded to Hefei.

sentences.zh: 先是，右軍司馬胡景略等攻合肥，久未下，睿按山川，夜，帥眾堰肥水，頃之，堰成水通，舟艦繼至。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hu Jinglue, Right Army Major, and others had attacked Hefei but long failed to take it. Rui surveyed the mountains and rivers; at night he led the crowd to dam the Fei River; soon the dam was complete and water flowed through; warships arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hu Jinglue, Right Army Major, and others had attacked Hefei but long failed to take it. Rui surveyed the terrain; at night he led his troops to dam the Fei River; soon the dam was complete and water flowed through; warships arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 魏築東、西小城夾合肥，睿先攻二城，魏將楊靈胤帥眾五萬奄至。

translations.literal: Wei built eastern and western small cities flanking Hefei; Rui first attacked the two cities; the Wei general Yang Lingyin led fifty thousand men and suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Wei built eastern and western outworks flanking Hefei; Rui first attacked the two outworks; the Wei general Yang Lingyin led fifty thousand men and suddenly arrived.

sentences.zh: 眾懼不敵，請奏益兵，睿笑曰：「賊至城下，方求益兵，將何所及！

translations.literal: The crowd feared they could not match them and asked to memorialize for more troops. Rui laughed and said: "The bandits have reached the walls and only now you ask for more troops—what good will that do!
translations.idiomatic: His men feared they could not match the enemy and asked to request reinforcements. Rui laughed and said: "The enemy has reached the walls and only now you ask for more troops—what good will that do!

sentences.zh: 且吾求益兵，彼亦益兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, if we ask for more troops, they too will add troops.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if we ask for reinforcements, they too will add troops.

sentences.zh: 兵貴用奇，豈在眾也！」

translations.literal: In warfare what is prized is the use of surprise—how does it lie in numbers!"
translations.idiomatic: In warfare what is prized is surprise—what does it matter how many men you have!"

sentences.zh: 遂擊靈胤，破之。

translations.literal: He then attacked Lingyin and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Lingyin and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 睿使軍主王懷靜築城於岸以守堰，魏攻拔之，城中千餘人皆沒。

translations.literal: Rui had Army Commander Wang Huaijing build a city on the bank to guard the dam; Wei attacked and took it; more than a thousand men in the city all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had Army Commander Wang Huaijing build a fort on the bank to guard the dam; Wei attacked and took it; more than a thousand men in the fort perished.

sentences.zh: 魏人乘勝至堤下，兵勢甚盛，諸將欲退還漅湖，或欲保三叉，睿怒曰：「寧有此邪！」

translations.literal: The Wei men pressed their victory to the foot of the dam; their military momentum was very strong; the generals wished to retreat to Chaohu Lake or to hold Sancha. Rui angrily said: "How can there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops pressed their victory to the foot of the dam; their momentum was overwhelming; the generals wished to retreat to Chaohu Lake or hold Sancha. Rui angrily said: "How can there be such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 命取傘扇麾幢，樹之堤下，示無動志。

translations.literal: He ordered umbrellas, fans, banners, and pennants taken and planted below the dam to show they had no intention of moving.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered umbrellas, fans, banners, and pennants brought and planted below the dam to show they had no intention of retreating.

sentences.zh: 魏人來鑿堤，睿親與之爭，魏兵卻，因築壘於堤以自固。

translations.literal: The Wei men came to breach the dam; Rui personally contended with them; the Wei troops withdrew, and he then built ramparts on the dam to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops came to breach the dam; Rui personally fought them off; the Wei troops withdrew, and he then built ramparts on the dam to secure his position.

sentences.zh: 睿起鬥艦，高與合肥城等，四面臨之，城中人皆哭，守將社元倫登城督戰，中弩死。

translations.literal: Rui raised tower ships as high as the walls of Hefei and pressed in on all four sides; the people in the city all wept; the defending general Du Yuanlun mounted the wall to direct the battle and was killed by a crossbow bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Rui raised tower ships as high as the walls of Hefei and pressed in on all four sides; the people in the city all wept; the defending general Du Yuanlun mounted the wall to direct the battle and was killed by a crossbow bolt.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，城潰，俘斬萬餘級，獲牛馬以萬數。

translations.literal: On xinsi the city collapsed; more than ten thousand were captured or beheaded; cattle and horses were taken by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the city fell; more than ten thousand were captured or killed; cattle and horses were taken by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 睿體素羸，未嘗跨馬，每戰，常乘板輿督厲將士，勇氣無敵；

translations.literal: Rui's body was always frail; he never mounted a horse; in every battle he rode a wooden litter to urge on the generals and soldiers—his courage was unmatched;
translations.idiomatic: Rui's body was always frail; he never mounted a horse; in every battle he rode in a wooden litter to urge on his generals and soldiers—his courage was unmatched;

sentences.zh: 晝接賓旅，夜半起，算軍書，張燈達曙。

translations.literal: by day he received guests and travelers; at midnight he rose to reckon military documents, lamps burning until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: by day he received guests and travelers; at midnight he rose to reckon military documents, lamps burning until dawn.

sentences.zh: 撫扦其眾，常如不及，故投募之士爭歸之。

translations.literal: He comforted and supported his troops as though he could never do enough; therefore volunteers competed to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted and supported his troops as though he could never do enough; therefore volunteers competed to join him.

sentences.zh: 所至頓捨，館宇籓牆，皆應準繩。

translations.literal: Wherever he halted, lodges and fence walls all met the standard measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he halted, lodges and fence walls all met the standard measure.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進至東陵，有詔班師。

translations.literal: The armies advanced to Dongling; there was an edict to withdraw the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The armies advanced to Dongling; an edict ordered withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 去魏城既近，諸將恐其追躡，睿悉遣輜重居前，身乘小輿殿後，魏人服睿威名，望之不敢逼，全軍而還。

translations.literal: They were already close to Wei territory; the generals feared pursuit. Rui sent all baggage trains ahead and himself rode a small litter in the rear; the Wei men respected Rui's martial renown and, seeing him, did not dare press close; the whole army returned intact.
