translations.idiomatic: They were already close to Wei territory; the generals feared pursuit. Rui sent all baggage trains ahead and himself rode in a small litter in the rear; the Wei troops respected Rui's renown and, seeing him, did not dare press close; the whole army returned intact.

sentences.zh: 於是遷豫州治合肥。

translations.literal: Thereupon the seat of Yuzhou was moved to Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the seat of Yuzhou was moved to Hefei.

sentences.zh: 壬午，魏遣尚書元遙南拒梁兵。

translations.literal: On renwu Wei dispatched Yuan Yao of the Secretariat south to resist the Liang army.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Wei dispatched Yuan Yao of the Secretariat south to resist the Liang army.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏遣征西將軍於勁節度秦、隴諸軍。

translations.literal: On guiwei Wei dispatched Yu Jin, General Who Campaigns West, to command all armies in Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Wei dispatched Yu Jin, General Who Campaigns West, to command all armies in Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，廬江太守聞喜裴邃克魏羊石城，庚寅，又克霍丘城。

translations.literal: On dinghai Pei Sui of Wenxi, Administrator of Lujiang, took Wei's Yangshi city; on gengyin he also took Huoqiu city.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Pei Sui of Wenxi, Administrator of Lujiang, took Wei's Yangshi city; on gengyin he also took Huoqiu city.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，青、冀二州刺史桓和克朐山城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengzi Huan He, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, took Qushan city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengzi Huan He, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, took Qushan city.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，魏安西將軍元麗擊王灋智，破之，斬首六千級。

translations.literal: On yisi Yuan Li, General Who Pacifies the West in Wei, attacked Wang Fazhi, defeated him, and beheaded six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Yuan Li, General Who Pacifies the West in Wei, attacked Wang Fazhi, defeated him, and beheaded six thousand.

sentences.zh: 張惠紹與假徐州刺史宋黑水陸俱進，趣彭城，圍高塚戍，魏武衛將軍奚康生將兵救之，丁未，惠紹兵不利，黑戰死。

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao and Song Hei, Acting Inspector of Xuzhou, advanced together by land and water toward Pengcheng and besieged the Gaozhong garrison; Xi Kangsheng, General of the Martial Guard in Wei, led troops to rescue it; on dingwei Huishao's army fared ill and Hei died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huishao and Song Hei, Acting Inspector of Xuzhou, advanced together by land and water toward Pengcheng and besieged the Gaozhong garrison; Xi Kangsheng, General of the Martial Guard in Wei, led troops to rescue it; on dingwei Huishao's army was defeated and Hei was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 太子統生五歲，能遍誦《五經》；

translations.literal: The Crown Prince Tong at age five could recite all the Five Classics;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince Tong at age five could recite all the Five Classics;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，始自禁中山居東宮。

translations.literal: on gengxu he first left Zhongshan to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: on gengxu he first left Zhongshan to reside in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏以度支尚書邢巒都督東討諸軍事。

translations.literal: On dingsi Wei made Xing Luan, Director of the Secretariat for Revenue, Supervisor of all eastern punitive military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Wei made Xing Luan, Director of the Secretariat for Revenue, Supervisor of all eastern punitive military affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏驃騎大將軍馮翊惠公源懷卒。

translations.literal: Yuan Huai, General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Fenyang in Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huai, General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Fenyang in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 懷性寬簡，不喜煩碎，常曰：「為貴人當舉綱維，何必事事詳細！

translations.literal: Huai's nature was broad and simple; he did not like trivial detail and often said: "As a noble one should raise the main ropes—why must every matter be detailed!
translations.idiomatic: Huai's nature was broad and simple; he did not like trivial detail and often said: "As a noble one should grasp the main ropes—why must every matter be detailed!

sentences.zh: 譬如為屋，但外望高顯，楹棟平正，基壁完牢，足矣；

translations.literal: It is like building a house: outwardly it should look tall and prominent, pillars and beams level and straight, foundation and walls complete and solid—that is enough;
translations.idiomatic: It is like building a house: outwardly it should look tall and prominent, pillars and beams level and straight, foundation and walls complete and solid—that is enough;

sentences.zh: 斧斤不平，斫削不密，非屋之病也。」

translations.literal: if hatchets are uneven or hewing not tight, that is not the house's fault."
translations.idiomatic: if hatchets are uneven or hewing not tight, that is not the house's fault."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅，桓和擊魏兗州，拔固城。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin Huan He attacked Yanzhou in Wei and took Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin Huan He attacked Yanzhou in Wei and took Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 呂苟兒率眾十餘萬屯孤山，圍逼秦州，元麗進擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Lü Gou'er led a host of more than a hundred thousand and encamped at Gushan, pressing Qinzhou; Yuan Li advanced to attack and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gou'er led more than a hundred thousand men and encamped at Gushan, pressing Qinzhou; Yuan Li advanced to attack and routed him.

sentences.zh: 行秦州事李韶掩擊孤山，獲其父母妻子，庚辰，苟兒帥其徒詣麗降。

translations.literal: Li Shao, acting for Qinzhou affairs, made a surprise attack on Gushan and captured Gou'er's parents, wife, and children; on gengchen Gou'er led his followers to Yuan Li to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao, acting for Qinzhou affairs, made a surprise attack on Gushan and captured Gou'er's parents, wife, and children; on gengchen Gou'er led his followers to Yuan Li to surrender.

sentences.zh: 兼太僕卿楊椿別討陳瞻，瞻據險拒守。

translations.literal: Yang Chun, Concurrent Director of the Imperial Stud, separately suppressed Chen Zhan; Zhan held the perilous terrain and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun, Concurrent Director of the Imperial Stud, separately suppressed Chen Zhan; Zhan held the perilous terrain and resisted.

sentences.zh: 諸將或請伏兵山蹊，斷其出入，待糧盡而攻之，或欲斬木焚山，然後進討。

translations.literal: Some generals asked to set ambush on mountain paths and cut off his coming and going, waiting until grain was exhausted to attack; others wished to cut trees and burn the mountains, then advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Some generals asked to set ambush on mountain paths and cut off his routes, waiting until grain was exhausted to attack; others wished to cut trees and burn the mountains, then advance to attack.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「皆非計也。

translations.literal: Chun said: "None of these are plans.
translations.idiomatic: Chun said: "None of these will work.

sentences.zh: 自官軍之至，所向輒克，賊所以深竄，正避死耳。

translations.literal: Since the government army arrived, wherever it went it prevailed; the reason the bandits burrow deep is precisely to avoid death.
translations.idiomatic: Since the government army arrived, wherever it went it prevailed; the reason the rebels burrow deep is precisely to avoid death.

sentences.zh: 今約勒諸軍，勿更侵掠，賊必謂我見險不前；

translations.literal: Now restrain the armies from further raiding; the bandits will surely think we see the peril and dare not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Now restrain the armies from further raiding; the rebels will surely think we see the peril and dare not advance;

sentences.zh: 待其無備，然後奮擊，可一舉平也。」

translations.literal: wait until they are unprepared, then strike with force— they can be pacified in one blow."
translations.idiomatic: wait until they are unprepared, then strike with force—they can be pacified in one blow."

sentences.zh: 乃止屯不進。

translations.literal: He then halted encampment and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He then halted and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 賊果出抄掠，椿復以馬畜餌之，不加討逐。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came out to raid; Chun again used horses and livestock to bait them and did not pursue or punish.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels indeed came out to raid; Chun again used horses and livestock to bait them and did not pursue.

sentences.zh: 久之，陰簡精卒，銜枚夜襲之，斬瞻，傳首。

translations.literal: After a long while he secretly selected elite troops, who held sticks in their mouths for a night assault, beheaded Zhan, and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he secretly selected elite troops for a night assault with gag-sticks in their mouths, beheaded Zhan, and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 秦、涇二州皆平。

translations.literal: Qin and Jing provinces were both pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Jing provinces were both pacified.

sentences.zh: 戊子，徐州刺史王伯敖與魏中山王英戰於陰陵，伯敖兵敗，失亡五千餘人。

translations.literal: On wuzi Wang Bo'ao, Inspector of Xuzhou, fought the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei at Yinling; Bo'ao's army was defeated and lost more than five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Wang Bo'ao, Inspector of Xuzhou, fought the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei at Yinling; Bo'ao's army was defeated and lost more than five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏發定、冀、瀛、相、並、肆六州十萬人以益南行之兵。

translations.literal: On jichou Wei mobilized a hundred thousand men from the six provinces of Ding, Ji, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Xi to augment the army marching south.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Wei mobilized a hundred thousand men from the six provinces of Ding, Ji, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Xi to augment the army marching south.

sentences.zh: 上遣將軍角念將兵一萬屯蒙山，招納兗州之民，降者甚眾。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched General Jiao Nian to lead ten thousand troops to garrison Mengshan and recruit the people of Yanzhou; those who surrendered were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched General Jiao Nian to lead ten thousand troops to garrison Mengshan and recruit the people of Yanzhou; very many surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是時，將軍蕭及屯固城，桓和屯孤山。

translations.literal: At this time General Xiao Ji garrisoned Gucheng and Huan He garrisoned Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: At this time General Xiao Ji garrisoned Gucheng and Huan He garrisoned Gushan.

sentences.zh: 魏邢巒遣統軍樊魯攻和，別將元恆攻及，統軍畢祖朽攻念。

translations.literal: Xing Luan of Wei dispatched Commander Fan Lu to attack He, Separate Commander Yuan Heng to attack Ji, and Commander Bi Zuxiu to attack Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan of Wei dispatched Commander Fan Lu to attack He, Separate Commander Yuan Heng to attack Ji, and Commander Bi Zuxiu to attack Nian.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魯大破和於孤山，恆拔固城，祖配擊念，走之。

translations.literal: On renyin Lu greatly defeated He at Gushan; Heng took Gucheng; Zuxiu attacked Nian and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Lu routed He at Gushan; Heng took Gucheng; Zuxiu attacked Nian and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏詔平南將軍安樂王詮督後發諸軍赴淮南。

translations.literal: On jiyou Wei ordered Yuan Xuan, General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Anle, to supervise the later-dispatched armies going to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Wei ordered Yuan Xuan, General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Anle, to supervise the later-dispatched armies going to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 詮，長樂之子也。

translations.literal: Xuan was the son of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was the son of Changle.

sentences.zh: 將軍藍懷恭與魏邢蠻戰於睢口，懷恭敗績，巒進圍宿預。

translations.literal: General Lan Huaigong fought Xing Man of Wei at Suikou; Huaigong was defeated; Luan advanced to besiege Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: General Lan Huaigong fought Xing Luan of Wei at Suikou; Huaigong was defeated; Luan advanced to besiege Suyu.

sentences.zh: 懷恭復於清南築城，巒與平南將軍楊大眼合攻之，九月，癸酉，拔之，斬懷恭，殺獲萬計。

translations.literal: Huaigong again built a city at Qingnan; Luan and Yang Dayan, General Who Pacifies the South, jointly attacked it; in the ninth month, on guiyou, they took it, beheaded Huaigong, and killed or captured men by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Huaigong again built a city at Qingnan; Luan and Yang Dayan, General Who Pacifies the South, jointly attacked it; in the ninth month, on guiyou, they took it, beheaded Huaigong, and killed or captured men by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 張惠紹棄宿預，蕭昺棄淮陽，遁還。

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao abandoned Suyu; Xiao Bing abandoned Huaiyang and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huishao abandoned Suyu; Xiao Bing abandoned Huaiyang and fled back.

sentences.zh: 臨川王宏以帝弟將兵，器械精新，軍容甚盛，北人以為百數十年所未之有。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linchuan, Hong, as the emperor's younger brother commanding troops, had weapons refined and new and military appearance very grand; northerners considered it something not seen for a hundred and some decades.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Linchuan, Hong, as the emperor's younger brother commanding troops, had refined new weapons and a magnificent army; northerners considered it something not seen for more than a century.

sentences.zh: 軍次洛口，前軍克梁城，諸將欲乘勝深入，宏性懦怯，部分乖方。

translations.literal: The army halted at Luokou; the forward army took Liangcheng; the generals wished to press the victory in depth; Hong's nature was timid and cowardly and his dispositions were awry.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Luokou; the forward army took Liangcheng; the generals wished to press the victory in depth; Hong's nature was timid and cowardly and his dispositions were awry.

sentences.zh: 魏詔邢巒引兵渡淮，與中山王英合攻梁城。

translations.literal: Wei ordered Xing Luan to lead troops across the Huai and join the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, in attacking Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ordered Xing Luan to lead troops across the Huai and join the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, in attacking Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 宏聞之，懼，召諸將議旋師。

translations.literal: Hong heard of this, was afraid, and summoned the generals to discuss withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Hong heard of this, was afraid, and summoned the generals to discuss withdrawing the army.

sentences.zh: 呂僧珍曰：「知難而退，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: Lü Sengzhen said: "To know difficulty and withdraw—is this not good!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sengzhen said: "To know difficulty and withdraw—is this not wise!"

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「我亦以為然。」

translations.literal: Hong said: "I too think so."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said: "I too think so."

sentences.zh: 柳惔曰：「自我大眾所臨，何城不服，何謂難乎！」

translations.literal: Liu Yan said: "Since our great host has arrived, what city has not submitted—what is called difficulty!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan said: "Since our great host has arrived, what city has not submitted—what difficulty is there!"

sentences.zh: 裴邃曰：「是行也，固敵是求，何難之避！」

translations.literal: Pei Sui said: "On this expedition we surely seek the enemy—why avoid difficulty!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui said: "On this expedition we surely seek the enemy—why speak of avoiding difficulty!"

sentences.zh: 馬仙玭曰：「王安得亡國之言！

translations.literal: Ma Xianbi said: "Your Highness, how can you utter words of a state's ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xianbi said: "Your Highness, how can you utter words fit for a ruined state!

sentences.zh: 天子掃境內以屬王，有前死一尺，無卻生一寸！」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has swept the realm within the borders and entrusted it to Your Highness—better to die advancing a foot than retreat living an inch!"
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has swept the realm within the borders and entrusted it to Your Highness—better to die advancing a foot than retreat living an inch!"

sentences.zh: 昌義之怒，鬚髮盡磔，曰：「呂僧珍可斬也！

translations.literal: Chang Yizhi was angry, his beard and hair all bristling, and said: "Lü Sengzhen should be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi was furious, his beard and hair bristling, and said: "Lü Sengzhen should be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 豈有百萬之師出未逢敵，望風遽退！

translations.literal: How can an army of a million go forth, not yet meet the enemy, and at rumor of wind hastily retreat!
translations.idiomatic: How can an army of a million go forth, not yet meet the enemy, and flee at the first rumor of attack!

sentences.zh: 何而目得見聖主乎！」

translations.literal: With what face can we see the sage sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: With what face can we see the sage sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 朱僧勇、胡辛生拔劍而退，曰：「欲退自退，下官當前向取死。」

translations.literal: Zhu Sengyong and Hu Xinsheng drew their swords and withdrew, saying: "If you wish to retreat, retreat yourselves—this subordinate will go forward to seek death."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Sengyong and Hu Xinsheng drew their swords and withdrew, saying: "If you wish to retreat, retreat yourselves—this subordinate will go forward to seek death."

sentences.zh: 議者罷出，僧珍謝諸將曰：「殿下昨來風動，意不在軍，深恐大致沮喪，故欲全師而返耳。」

translations.literal: When the council dispersed, Sengzhen apologized to the generals: "Yesterday His Highness's mind was unsettled and his intent was not on the army; I deeply feared the great host would be discouraged, and therefore wished to preserve the army and return."
translations.idiomatic: When the council dispersed, Sengzhen apologized to the generals: "Yesterday His Highness's mind was unsettled and his intent was not on the army; I deeply feared the great host would be discouraged, and therefore wished to preserve the army and return."

sentences.zh: 宏不敢遽違群議，停軍不前。

translations.literal: Hong did not dare immediately defy the collective opinion and halted the army without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong did not dare immediately defy the collective opinion and halted the army without advancing.

sentences.zh: 魏人知其不武，遺以巾幗，且歌之曰：「不畏蕭娘與呂姥，但畏合肥有韋虎。」

translations.literal: The Wei men knew he was not martial; they sent him women's headgear and also sang: "We do not fear Lady Xiao and Old Mother Lü, but only fear that at Hefei there is Tiger Wei."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei men knew he was not martial; they sent him women's headgear and also sang: "We do not fear Lady Xiao and Old Mother Lü, but only fear that at Hefei there is Tiger Wei."

sentences.zh: 虎，謂韋睿也。

translations.literal: Tiger means Wei Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger means Wei Rui.

sentences.zh: 僧珍歎曰：「使始興、吳平為帥而佐之，豈有為敵人所侮如是乎！」

translations.literal: Sengzhen sighed and said: "If Shixing and Wuping were commanders and assisted him, how could he be insulted by the enemy like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen sighed and said: "If Shixing and Wuping were commanders and assisted him, how could he be insulted by the enemy like this!"

sentences.zh: 欲遣裴邃分軍取壽陽，大眾停洛口，宏固執不聽，令軍中曰：「人馬有前行者斬！」

translations.literal: He wished to dispatch Pei Sui with a separate army to take Shouyang while the great host remained at Luokou; Hong obstinately would not listen and ordered in the army: "Whoever advances man or horse ahead—behead!"
translations.idiomatic: He wished to dispatch Pei Sui with a separate army to take Shouyang while the great host remained at Luokou; Hong obstinately would not listen and ordered in the army: "Whoever advances ahead—behead!"

sentences.zh: 於是將士人懷憤怒。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and soldiers all harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officers and soldiers all harbored anger.

sentences.zh: 魏奚康生馳遣楊大眼謂中山王英曰：「梁人自克梁城已後，久不進軍，其勢可見，必畏我也。

translations.literal: Xi Kangsheng of Wei swiftly sent Yang Dayan to tell the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying: "Since the Liang men took Liangcheng they have long not advanced—their momentum can be seen; they surely fear us.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kangsheng of Wei swiftly sent Yang Dayan to tell the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying: "Since the Liang men took Liangcheng they have long not advanced—their momentum shows they surely fear us.

sentences.zh: 王若進據洛水，彼自奔敗。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness advances and holds the Luo River, they will flee in defeat of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness advances and holds the Luo River, they will flee in defeat of themselves."

sentences.zh: 英曰：「蕭臨川雖騃，其下有良將韋、裴之屬，未可輕也。

translations.literal: Ying said: "Although Xiao of Linchuan is dull, beneath him are fine generals like Wei and Pei and their kind—not to be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Ying said: "Although Xiao of Linchuan is dull, beneath him are fine generals like Wei and Pei and their kind—not to be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 宜且觀形勢，勿與交鋒。

translations.literal: It is fitting first to observe the situation and not cross blades.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting first to observe the situation and not join battle.

sentences.zh: 張惠紹號令嚴明，所至獨克，軍於下邳，下邳人多欲降者，惠紹諭之曰：「我若得城，諸卿皆是國人，若不能克，徒使諸卿失鄉里，非朝廷弔民之意也。

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao's orders were strict and clear; wherever he went he alone prevailed. His army was at Xiapi; many of the people of Xiapi wished to surrender. Huishao instructed them: "If I take the city, you all will be citizens of our state; if I cannot take it, I would only make you lose your homelands—this is not the court's intent to comfort the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huishao's orders were strict and clear; wherever he went he alone prevailed. His army was at Xiapi; many of the people of Xiapi wished to surrender. Huishao instructed them: "If I take the city, you all will be citizens of our state; if I cannot take it, I would only make you lose your homelands—this is not the court's intent to comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 今且安堵復業，勿妄自辛苦。」

translations.literal: For now settle peacefully and resume your occupations; do not trouble yourselves in vain."
translations.idiomatic: For now settle peacefully and resume your occupations; do not trouble yourselves in vain."

sentences.zh: 降人鹹悅。

translations.literal: The surrendering people were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendering people were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 己丑，夜，洛口暴風雨，軍中驚，臨川王宏與數騎逃去。

translations.literal: On jichou, at night, a violent wind and rain struck Luokou; the army was alarmed; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, fled with several horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, at night, a violent storm struck Luokou; the army panicked; the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, fled with several horsemen.

sentences.zh: 將士求宏不得，皆散歸，棄甲投戈，填滿水陸，捐棄病者及羸老，死者近五萬人。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers could not find Hong and all dispersed homeward; they cast off armor and threw down weapons, filling land and water; the sick and weak elderly were abandoned; the dead approached fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers could not find Hong and all dispersed homeward; they cast off armor and threw down weapons, filling land and water; the sick and weak elderly were abandoned; the dead approached fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 宏乘小船濟江，夜至白石壘，叩城門求入。

translations.literal: Hong rode a small boat across the river; at night he reached the Baishi fortress and knocked on the gate seeking entry.
translations.idiomatic: Hong rode a small boat across the river; at night he reached the Baishi fortress and knocked on the gate seeking entry.

sentences.zh: 臨汝侯淵猷登城謂曰：「百萬之師，一朝鳥散，國之存亡，未可知也。

translations.literal: Yuan You, Marquis of Linru, mounted the wall and said: "An army of a million dispersed in a morning like birds—the state's survival or ruin is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan You, Marquis of Linru, mounted the wall and said: "An army of a million dispersed in a morning like birds—the state's survival or ruin is not yet known.

sentences.zh: 恐奸人乘間為變，城不可夜開。」

translations.literal: I fear treacherous men may seize the interval to make trouble; the gate cannot be opened at night."
translations.idiomatic: I fear treacherous men may seize the moment to make trouble; the gate cannot be opened at night."

sentences.zh: 宏無以對，乃縋食饋之。

translations.literal: Hong had nothing to reply and had food lowered to feed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had nothing to reply and had food lowered to feed him.

sentences.zh: 淵猷，淵藻之弟。

translations.literal: Yuan You was the younger brother of Yuanzao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan You was the younger brother of Yuanzao.

sentences.zh: 時昌義之軍梁城，聞洛口敗，與張惠紹皆引兵退。

translations.literal: At the time Chang Yizhi's army was at Liangcheng; hearing of the defeat at Luokou, he and Zhang Huishao both led their troops back.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chang Yizhi's army was at Liangcheng; hearing of the defeat at Luokou, he and Zhang Huishao both led their troops back.

sentences.zh: 魏主詔中山王英乘勝平蕩東南，遂北至馬頭，攻拔之，城中糧儲，魏悉遷之歸北。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign ordered the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, to follow up victory and pacify the southeast; he then went north to Matou, attacked and took it, and all grain stores in the city Wei moved back north.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor ordered the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, to follow up his victory and pacify the southeast; he then went north to Matou, took it, and moved all grain stores in the city back north.

sentences.zh: 議者鹹曰：「魏運米北歸，當不復南向。」

translations.literal: Those in council all said: "Wei is moving grain north—surely they will not again turn south."
translations.idiomatic: Those in council all said: "Wei is moving grain north—they surely will not turn south again."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不然，此必欲進兵，為詐計耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so—this is surely intending to advance troops; it is a ruse."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Not so—this is surely a ruse to cover an advance."

sentences.zh: 乃命修鐘離城，敕昌義之為戰守之備。

translations.literal: He then ordered Zhongli city repaired and instructed Chang Yizhi to make preparations for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Zhongli city repaired and instructed Chang Yizhi to prepare for battle and defense.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，英進圍鐘離，魏主詔邢巒引兵會之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Ying advanced to besiege Zhongli; the Wei sovereign ordered Xing Luan to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Ying advanced to besiege Zhongli; the Wei emperor ordered Xing Luan to lead troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 巒上表，以為：「南軍雖野戰非敵，而城守有餘，今盡銳攻鐘離，得之則所利無幾，不得則虧損甚大。

translations.literal: Luan memorialized, stating: "The southern army, though not a match in field battle, has more than enough for city defense; now to concentrate elite forces on Zhongli—if taken, the profit is slight; if not taken, the loss is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized, stating: "The southern army, though not a match in field battle, is more than adequate for defense; now to concentrate elite forces on Zhongli—if taken, the profit is slight; if not taken, the loss is very great.

sentences.zh: 且介在淮外，借使束手歸順，猶恐無糧難守，況殺士卒以攻之乎！

translations.literal: Moreover it lies beyond the Huai; even if they submitted with hands bound, I still fear it would be hard to hold without grain—how much more to kill soldiers attacking it!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it lies beyond the Huai; even if they submitted willingly, I still fear it would be hard to hold without grain—how much more to kill soldiers attacking it!

sentences.zh: 又，征南士卒從戎二時，疲弊死傷，不問可知。

translations.literal: Again, the Campaign South soldiers have been at war two seasons; weariness, injury, and death need not be asked to be known.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Campaign South soldiers have been at war two seasons; their weariness, injury, and death need no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 雖有乘勝之資，懼無可用之力。

translations.literal: Though there is the resource of riding victory, I fear there is no usable strength.
translations.idiomatic: Though we have the momentum of victory, I fear we lack usable strength.

sentences.zh: 若臣愚見，謂宜修復舊戍，撫循諸州，以俟後舉，江東之釁，不患其無。」

translations.literal: In this servant's foolish view, it is fitting to restore old garrisons, comfort and guide the provinces, and await a later campaign—the troubles of Jiangdong, one need not worry they will be lacking."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, it is fitting to restore old garrisons, comfort and guide the provinces, and await a later campaign—the troubles of Jiangdong will surely come in time."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「濟淮掎角，事如前敕，何容猶爾盤桓，方有此請！

translations.literal: An edict said: "Crossing the Huai in pincer coordination was as in the previous order—how can you still linger thus and now make this request!
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Crossing the Huai in coordinated pincer attack was as in the previous order—how can you still linger and now make this request!

sentences.zh: 可速進軍！」

translations.literal: Advance the army swiftly!"
translations.idiomatic: Advance the army at once!"

sentences.zh: 巒又表，以為：「今中山進軍鐘離，實所未解。

translations.literal: Luan memorialized again, stating: "Now the Prince of Zhongshan advances on Zhongli—I truly do not understand it.
translations.idiomatic: Luan memorialized again, stating: "Now the Prince of Zhongshan advances on Zhongli—I truly do not understand it.

sentences.zh: 若為得失之計，不顧萬全，直襲廣陵，出其不備，或未可知。

translations.literal: If for a calculation of gain and loss, disregarding complete safety, one struck straight at Guangling and caught them unprepared—that might be unknown.
translations.idiomatic: If for a calculation of gain and loss, disregarding complete safety, one struck straight at Guangling and caught them unprepared—that might succeed.

sentences.zh: 若正欲以八十日糧取鐘離城者，臣未之前聞也。

translations.literal: If one truly wishes to take Zhongli city with only eighty days' grain, I have never heard of it before.
translations.idiomatic: If one truly wishes to take Zhongli city with only eighty days' grain, I have never heard of such a thing.

sentences.zh: 彼堅城自守。

translations.literal: They hold a strong city and defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They hold a strong city and defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 不與人戰，城塹水深，非可填塞，空坐至春，士卒自弊。

translations.literal: They do not fight men; moat and ramparts are deep in water—not to be filled; sitting idle until spring, the soldiers will wear themselves out.
translations.idiomatic: They will not come out to fight; the moat and ramparts are deep with water and cannot be filled; sitting idle until spring, our soldiers will wear themselves out.

sentences.zh: 若遣臣赴彼，從何致糧！

translations.literal: If I am sent thither, whence shall grain be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: If I am sent there, whence shall grain be obtained!

sentences.zh: 夏來之兵，不繼冬服，脫遇冰雪，何方取濟！

translations.literal: Soldiers who came in summer have no winter clothing to follow; if they meet ice and snow, whence relief!
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who came in summer have no winter clothing; if they meet ice and snow, whence shall relief come!

sentences.zh: 臣寧荷怯懦不進之責，不受敗損空行之罪。

translations.literal: I would rather bear the blame of cowardice in not advancing than accept the crime of defeat and loss in an empty march.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather bear the blame of cowardice in not advancing than accept the crime of defeat in a futile march.

sentences.zh: 鐘離天險，朝貴所具，若有內應，則所不知；

translations.literal: Zhongli is a heaven-sent barrier, furnished by the court's nobles; if there is internal collusion, that I do not know;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli is a heaven-sent barrier, furnished by the court's nobles; if there is internal collusion, that I do not know;

sentences.zh: 如其無也，必無克狀。

translations.literal: if there is none, there will surely be no prospect of taking it.
translations.idiomatic: if there is none, there will surely be no prospect of taking it.

sentences.zh: 若信臣言，願賜臣停，若謂臣憚行求還，臣所領兵盡付中山，任其處分，臣止以單騎隨之東西。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty trusts my words, I beg to be granted a halt; if you say I fear the march and seek return, I will give all the troops I command to the Prince of Zhongshan for his disposal; I will only follow east and west on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty trusts my words, I beg to be granted a halt; if you say I fear the march and seek return, I will give all the troops I command to the Prince of Zhongshan for his disposal; I will only follow on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 臣屢更為將，頗知可否，臣既謂難，何容強遣！」

translations.literal: I have repeatedly been made a general and know fairly well what can and cannot be done; since I say it is difficult, how can I be forced to go!"
translations.idiomatic: I have repeatedly served as a general and know fairly well what can and cannot be done; since I say it is difficult, how can I be forced to go!"

sentences.zh: 乃召巒還，更命鎮東將軍蕭寶寅與英同圍鐘離。

translations.literal: He then summoned Luan back and instead ordered Xiao Baoyin, General Who Guards the East, to join Ying in besieging Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Luan back and instead ordered Xiao Baoyin, General Who Guards the East, to join Ying in besieging Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 侍中盧昶素惡巒，與侍中、領右衛將軍元暉共譖之，使御史中尉崔亮彈巒在漢中掠人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Lu Chang, Attendant-in-Ordinary, had long hated Luan; with Yuan Hui, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commander of the Right Guard, he slandered him together, having Imperial Inspecting Censor Cui Liang impeach Luan for seizing people as slaves in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang, Attendant-in-Ordinary, had long hated Luan; with Yuan Hui, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commander of the Right Guard, he slandered him together, having Imperial Inspecting Censor Cui Liang impeach Luan for seizing people as slaves in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 巒以漢中所得美女賂暉，暉言於魏主曰：「巒新有大功，不當以赦前小事案之。」

translations.literal: Luan used beautiful women obtained in Hanzhong to bribe Hui; Hui said to the Wei sovereign: "Luan has newly achieved great merit; he should not be prosecuted for a small matter before the amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Luan used beautiful women obtained in Hanzhong to bribe Hui; Hui said to the Wei emperor: "Luan has newly achieved great merit; he should not be prosecuted for a small matter before the amnesty."

sentences.zh: 魏主以為然，遂不問。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign thought it so and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor agreed and did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 暉與盧昶皆有寵於魏主，而貪縱，時人謂之「餓虎將軍」、「饑鷹侍中」。

translations.literal: Hui and Lu Chang were both favored by the Wei sovereign yet greedy and unrestrained; people of the time called them "the starving tiger general" and "the hungry hawk attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Lu Chang were both favored by the Wei emperor yet greedy and unrestrained; people of the time called them "the starving tiger general" and "the hungry hawk attendant."

sentences.zh: 暉尋遷吏部尚書，用官皆有定價，大郡二千匹，次郡、下郡遞減其半，餘官各有等差，選者謂之「市曹」。

translations.literal: Hui soon moved to Director of the Secretariat for Personnel; every office had a fixed price—great commanderies two thousand bolts, middle and lower commanderies decreasing by half in succession, other offices each with graded differences; selectors called it "the market bureau."
translations.idiomatic: Hui soon became Director of the Secretariat for Personnel; every office had a fixed price—great commanderies two thousand bolts, middle and lower commanderies decreasing by half in succession, other offices each with graded differences; selectors called it "the market bureau."

sentences.zh: 丁酉，梁兵圍義陽者夜遁，魏郢州刺史婁悅追擊，破之。

translations.literal: On dingyou the Liang troops besieging Yiyang fled by night; Lou Yue, Inspector of Yingzhou in Wei, pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Liang troops besieging Yiyang fled by night; Lou Yue, Inspector of Yingzhou in Wei, pursued and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 柔然庫者可汗卒，子伏圖立，號佗汗可汗，改元始平。

translations.literal: Kekhan, khaghan of the Rouran, died; his son Futulu succeeded, styled Tuo Khan, and changed the era name to Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Kekhan, khaghan of the Rouran, died; his son Futulu succeeded, styled Tuo Khan, and changed the era name to Shiping.

sentences.zh: 戊申，佗汗遣使者紇奚勿六跋如魏請和。

translations.literal: On wushen Tuo Khan dispatched the envoy Hexi Wuliu Ba to Wei to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Tuo Khan dispatched the envoy Hexi Wuliu Ba to Wei to seek peace.

sentences.zh: 魏主不報其使，謂勿六跋曰：「蠕蠕遠祖社侖，乃魏之叛臣，往者包容，暫聽通使。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign did not reply to his embassy and said to Wuliu Ba: "The distant ancestor of the Rouran, Shelun, was a rebel minister of Wei; in the past we tolerated and briefly allowed communication.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor did not reply to his embassy and said to Wuliu Ba: "The distant ancestor of the Rouran, Shelun, was a rebel minister of Wei; in the past we tolerated and briefly allowed communication.

sentences.zh: 今蠕蠕衰微，不及疇昔，大魏之德，方隆周、漢，正以江南未平，少寬北略，通和之事，未容相許。

translations.literal: Now the Rouran are weak and do not match former times; Great Wei's virtue is just rising like Zhou and Han; precisely because Jiangnan is not yet pacified, we slightly ease the northern campaign—matters of alliance cannot yet be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Rouran are weak and do not match former times; Great Wei's virtue is just rising like Zhou and Han; precisely because Jiangnan is not yet pacified, we slightly ease the northern campaign—matters of alliance cannot yet be granted.

sentences.zh: 若修籓禮，款誠昭著者，當不爾孤也。」

translations.literal: If you observe vassal ritual and your sincere good faith is manifest, I shall not leave you thus isolated."
translations.idiomatic: If you observe vassal ritual and your sincere good faith is manifest, I shall not leave you thus isolated."

sentences.zh: 魏京兆王愉、廣平王懷國臣多驕縱，公行屬請，魏主詔中尉崔亮究治之，坐死者三十餘人，其不死者悉除名為民。

translations.literal: The state ministers of the Princes of Jingzhao, Yu, and Guangping, Huai, in Wei were mostly arrogant and unrestrained, openly practicing patronage requests; the Wei sovereign ordered Censor Cui Liang to investigate; more than thirty were sentenced to death, and those not dead were all struck from the rolls and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The state ministers of the Princes of Jingzhao, Yu, and Guangping, Huai, in Wei were mostly arrogant and unrestrained, openly practicing patronage requests; the Wei emperor ordered Censor Cui Liang to investigate; more than thirty were sentenced to death, and those not executed were all struck from the rolls and made commoners.

sentences.zh: 惟廣平右常侍楊昱、文學崔楷以忠諫獲免。

translations.literal: Only Yang Yu, Right Regular Attendant of Guangping, and Cui Kai, Literary Scholar, were spared for loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Yu, Right Regular Attendant of Guangping, and Cui Kai, Literary Scholar, were spared for loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 昱，椿之子也。

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the son of Yang Chun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙丑，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yichou, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yichou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 詔右衛將軍曹景宗都督諸軍二十萬救鐘離。

translations.literal: An edict made Cao Jingzong, General of the Right Guard, Supervisor of all armies with two hundred thousand men to rescue Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Cao Jingzong, General of the Right Guard, to supervise two hundred thousand men to rescue Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 上敕景宗頓道人洲，俟眾軍齊集俱進。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jingzong to halt at Daoren Isle and wait until all armies were assembled before advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jingzong to halt at Daoren Isle and wait until all armies were assembled before advancing together.

sentences.zh: 景宗固啟求先據邵陽洲尾，上不許。

translations.literal: Jingzong obstinately memorialized asking first to hold the tail of Shaoyang Isle; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong obstinately memorialized asking first to hold the tail of Shaoyang Isle; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 景宗欲專其功，違詔而進，值暴風猝起，頗有溺者，復還守先頓。

translations.literal: Jingzong wished to monopolize the achievement, disobeyed the edict and advanced, met a sudden violent wind, and many were drowned; he returned to hold his former encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong wished to monopolize the credit, disobeyed the edict and advanced, met a sudden violent storm, and many were drowned; he returned to his former encampment.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，曰：「景宗不進，蓋天意也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and said: "Jingzong's not advancing is surely Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and said: "Jingzong's failure to advance was surely Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 若孤軍獨往，城不時立，必致狼狽。

translations.literal: If a lone army went alone and the city were not taken in time, it would surely lead to disgraceful straits.
translations.idiomatic: If a lone army went alone and the city were not taken in time, disaster would surely follow.

sentences.zh: 今破賊必矣。」

translations.literal: Now defeating the bandits is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Now we are certain to defeat the enemy."

sentences.zh: 初，漢歸義侯勢之末，群獠始出，北自漢中，南至邛、笮，佈滿山谷。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Marquis of Guyi Shi of Han, the Liao tribes first emerged; north from Hanzhong, south to Qiong and Zuo, they spread through mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of Marquis of Guyi Shi of Han, the Liao tribes first emerged; from Hanzhong in the north to Qiong and Zuo in the south, they spread through the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 勢既亡。

translations.literal: When Shi perished,
translations.idiomatic: When Shi perished,

sentences.zh: 蜀民多東徙，山谷空地皆為獠所據。

translations.literal: Shu people mostly moved east; empty lands in mountain valleys were all occupied by the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: many Shu people moved east; empty lands in the mountain valleys were all occupied by the Liao.

sentences.zh: 其近郡縣與華民雜居者，頗輸租賦，遠在深山者，郡縣不能制。

translations.literal: Those near commanderies and counties who lived mixed with Chinese mostly paid rents and levies; those far in deep mountains the commanderies and counties could not control.
translations.idiomatic: Those near commanderies and counties who lived mixed with Chinese mostly paid rents and levies; those far in the deep mountains the commanderies and counties could not control.

sentences.zh: 梁、益二州歲伐獠以自潤，公私利之。

translations.literal: Liang and Yi provinces annually raided the Liao for their own profit; public and private both benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Yi provinces annually raided the Liao for profit; public and private interests alike benefited.

sentences.zh: 及邢巒為梁州，獠近者皆安堵樂業，遠者不敢為寇。

translations.literal: When Xing Luan was in Liang province, nearby Liao all settled peacefully and pursued their occupations; those far off did not dare make raids.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Luan governed Liang province, nearby Liao all settled peacefully and pursued their occupations; those far off did not dare raid.

sentences.zh: 巒既罷去，魏以羊祉為梁州刺史，傅豎眼為益州刺史。

translations.literal: After Luan was removed, Wei made Yang Zhi Inspector of Liang province and Fu Shuyan Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan was removed, Wei made Yang Zhi Inspector of Liang province and Fu Shuyan Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祉性酷虐，不得物情。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was cruel and tyrannical; he did not win the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's nature was cruel and tyrannical; he did not win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 獠王趙清荊引梁兵入州境為寇，祉遣兵擊破之。

translations.literal: The Liao king Zhao Qingjing led Liang troops into the province as bandits; Zhi dispatched troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao king Zhao Qingjing led Liang troops into the province as raiders; Zhi dispatched troops and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 豎眼施恩布信，大得獠和。

translations.literal: Shuyan bestowed favor and spread trust; he greatly won the Liao's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan bestowed favor and spread trust; he greatly won the Liao's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸卯，都亭靖侯謝朏卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on guimao, Xie Tiao, Marquis of Duting, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guimao, Xie Tiao, Marquis of Duting, died.

sentences.zh: 魏人議樂，久不決。

translations.literal: The Wei people debated music but long could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court debated music but long could not reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝二天監六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, the Martial Sovereign, second scroll, sixth year of Tianjian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, sixth year of Tianjian (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元五零七年）

translations.literal: dinghai, 507 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dinghai, AD 507)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，公孫崇請委衛軍將軍、尚書右僕射高肇監其事；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Gongsun Chong asked that Gao Zhao, General of the Guard and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, supervise the matter;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Gongsun Chong asked that Gao Zhao, General of the Guard and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, supervise the matter;

sentences.zh: 魏主知肇不學，詔太常卿劉芳佐之。

translations.literal: the Wei sovereign knew Zhao was unlearned and ordered Liu Fang, Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices, to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei emperor knew Zhao was unlearned and ordered Liu Fang, Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices, to assist him.

sentences.zh: 魏中山王英與平東將軍楊大眼等眾數十萬攻鐘離。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei and Yang Dayan, General Who Pacifies the East, and others with a host of several hundred thousand attacked Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei and Yang Dayan, General Who Pacifies the East, and others with several hundred thousand men attacked Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 鐘離城北阻淮水，魏人於邵陽洲兩岸為橋，樹柵數百步，跨淮通道。

translations.literal: Zhongli city's north was blocked by the Huai; the Wei men built bridges on both banks of Shaoyang Isle, set palisades for several hundred paces, and spanned the Huai for passage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli city's north was blocked by the Huai; the Wei troops built bridges on both banks of Shaoyang Isle, set palisades for several hundred paces, and spanned the Huai for passage.

sentences.zh: 英據南岸攻城，大眼據北岸立城，以通糧運。

translations.literal: Ying held the south bank to attack the city; Dayan held the north bank and built a city to open grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Ying held the south bank to attack the city; Dayan held the north bank and built a fort to secure grain transport.

sentences.zh: 城中眾才三千人，昌義之督帥將士，隨方抗禦。

translations.literal: The crowd in the city was only three thousand; Chang Yizhi directed and led officers and soldiers, resisting according to each direction.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison numbered only three thousand; Chang Yizhi directed his officers and soldiers, resisting on every side.

sentences.zh: 魏人以車載土填塹，使其眾負土隨之，嚴騎蹙其後。

translations.literal: The Wei men used carts to carry earth to fill the moat, made their masses carry earth and follow, and strict cavalry pressed their rear.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops used carts to carry earth to fill the moat, made their men carry earth and follow, and strict cavalry pressed from the rear.

sentences.zh: 人有未及回者，因以土迮之。

translations.literal: Those who had not yet turned back were thus buried with earth.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had not yet turned back were buried alive under the earth.

sentences.zh: 俄而塹滿，沖車所撞，城土輒頹，義之用泥補之，沖車雖入而不能壞。

translations.literal: Soon the moat was full; where battering rams struck, city earth repeatedly collapsed; Yizhi patched it with mud; though the rams entered they could not destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the moat was full; where battering rams struck, the wall repeatedly collapsed; Yizhi patched it with mud; though the rams entered they could not breach it.

sentences.zh: 魏人晝夜苦攻，分番相代，墜而復升，莫有退者。

translations.literal: The Wei men attacked bitterly day and night, taking turns in relays; falling they climbed again—none retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops attacked bitterly day and night, taking turns in relays; falling they climbed again—none retreated.

sentences.zh: 一日戰數十合，前後殺傷萬計，魏人死者與城平。

translations.literal: In one day they fought several tens of rounds; killed and wounded before and after numbered in the tens of thousands; Wei dead were level with the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In one day they fought dozens of engagements; killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands; Wei dead piled level with the wall.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏主召英使還，英表稱：「臣志殄逋寇，而月初已來，霖雨不止，若三月晴霽，城必可克，願少賜寬假。」

translations.literal: In the second month the Wei sovereign summoned Ying to return; Ying memorialized: "My will is to exterminate the fleeing bandits, but since the month's beginning unceasing rain has fallen; if in the third month skies clear, the city can surely be taken—I beg a little extension."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Wei emperor summoned Ying to return; Ying memorialized: "My will is to exterminate the fleeing enemy, but since the month's beginning unceasing rain has fallen; if skies clear in the third month, the city can surely be taken—I beg a little more time."

sentences.zh: 魏主復賜詔曰：「彼土蒸濕，無宜久淹。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign again granted an edict: "That land is steamy and damp—not fitting to linger long.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor again granted an edict: "That land is steamy and damp—not fitting to linger long.

sentences.zh: 勢雖必取，乃將軍之深計，兵久力殆，亦朝廷之所憂也。」

translations.literal: Though the momentum must surely take it, that is the general's deep plan; troops long deployed, strength exhausted—that is also what the court worries over."
translations.idiomatic: Though victory is surely attainable, that is the general's deep plan; troops long deployed, strength exhausted—that is also what the court worries over."

sentences.zh: 英猶表稱必克，魏主遣步兵校尉范紹詣英議攻取形勢。

translations.literal: Ying still memorialized that he would surely take it; the Wei sovereign dispatched Fan Shao, Commandant of Footsoldiers, to go to Ying to discuss the situation for attack and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Ying still memorialized that he would surely take it; the Wei emperor dispatched Fan Shao, Commandant of Footsoldiers, to Ying to discuss the situation for attack and capture.

sentences.zh: 紹見鐘離城堅，勸英引還，英不從。

translations.literal: Shao saw Zhongli city was strong and urged Ying to withdraw; Ying did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shao saw Zhongli city was strong and urged Ying to withdraw; Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 上命豫州刺史韋睿將兵救鐘離，受曹景宗節度。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wei Rui, Inspector of Yuzhou, to lead troops to rescue Zhongli, under Cao Jingzong's command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wei Rui, Inspector of Yuzhou, to lead troops to rescue Zhongli, under Cao Jingzong's command.

sentences.zh: 睿自合肥取直道，由陰陵大澤行，值澗谷，輒飛橋以濟師。

translations.literal: Rui from Hefei took the direct route, traveling through the great marsh of Yinling; when he met streams and valleys he forthwith flew bridges to get the army across.
translations.idiomatic: Rui from Hefei took the direct route, traveling through the great marsh of Yinling; when he met streams and valleys he forthwith threw bridges across to get the army through.

sentences.zh: 人畏魏兵盛，多勸睿緩行。

translations.literal: People feared Wei troops were strong and many urged Rui to march slowly.
translations.idiomatic: People feared the Wei army was strong and many urged Rui to march slowly.

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「鐘離今鑿穴而處，負戶而汲，車馳卒奔，猶恐其後，而況緩乎！

translations.literal: Rui said: "Zhongli now dwells in dug caves, draws water bearing their doors on their backs; chariots gallop and soldiers run—we still fear being too late—how much more to go slowly!
translations.idiomatic: Rui said: "Zhongli now dwells in dug caves, draws water bearing their doors on their backs; chariots gallop and soldiers run—we still fear being too late—how much more to go slowly!

sentences.zh: 魏人已墮吾腹中，卿曹勿憂也。」

translations.literal: The Wei men have already fallen into our bellies—you all need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei men are already in our grasp—you all need not worry."

sentences.zh: 旬日至邵陽。

translations.literal: In ten days he reached Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In ten days he reached Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 上豫敕曹景宗曰：「韋睿，卿之鄉望，宜善敬之！」

translations.literal: The emperor beforehand ordered Cao Jingzong: "Wei Rui is a man of honor from your homeland—you should respect him well!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor beforehand ordered Cao Jingzong: "Wei Rui is a man of honor from your homeland—you should treat him with respect!"

sentences.zh: 景宗見睿，禮甚謹。

translations.literal: When Jingzong saw Rui, his courtesy was very careful.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong met Rui, his courtesy was most deferential.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，曰：「二將和，師必濟矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and said: "The two generals are in harmony—the army will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and said: "The two generals are in harmony—the army will surely succeed."

sentences.zh: 景宗與睿進頓邵陽洲，睿於景宗營前二十里夜掘長塹，樹鹿角，截洲為城，去魏城百餘步。

translations.literal: Jingzong and Rui advanced and halted at Shaoyang Isle; Rui at night twenty li before Jingzong's camp dug a long moat, set antlers, cut off the isle as a city, a hundred and some paces from the Wei city.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and Rui advanced and halted at Shaoyang Isle; Rui at night twenty li before Jingzong's camp dug a long moat, set antlers, cut off the isle as a fort, a hundred and some paces from the Wei camp.

sentences.zh: 南梁太守馮道根，能走馬步地，計馬足以賦功，比曉而營立。

translations.literal: Feng Daogen, Administrator of Nanliang, could run a horse to pace the ground, calculate horse paces to assign work, and by dawn the camp was established.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen, Administrator of Nanliang, could pace the ground on horseback, calculate the work by horse paces, and by dawn the camp was established.

sentences.zh: 魏中山王英大驚，以杖擊地曰：「是何神也！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei was greatly alarmed and struck the ground with his staff, saying: "What god is this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, of Wei was greatly alarmed and struck the ground with his staff, saying: "What sorcery is this!"

sentences.zh: 景宗等器甲精新，軍容甚盛，魏人望之奪氣。

translations.literal: Jingzong and the others had weapons and armor refined and new, military appearance very grand; the Wei men, seeing them, lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and the others had refined new weapons and armor and a magnificent army; the Wei troops, seeing them, lost heart.

sentences.zh: 景宗慮城中危懼，募軍士言文達等潛行水底，繼敕入城，城中始知有外援，勇氣百倍。

translations.literal: Jingzong feared peril and terror in the city; he recruited soldiers Yan Wenda and others to travel secretly underwater, continuing orders into the city; the city first knew there was external aid and their courage increased a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong feared panic in the city; he recruited soldiers Yan Wenda and others to travel secretly underwater with orders into the city; the garrison first learned there was external aid and their courage increased a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 楊大眼勇冠軍中，將萬餘騎來戰，所向皆靡。

translations.literal: Yang Dayan's courage topped the army; he led more than ten thousand horsemen to battle; wherever he went all were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayan's courage topped the army; he led more than ten thousand horsemen to battle; wherever he went all were swept away.

sentences.zh: 睿結車為陳，大眼聚騎圍之，睿以強弩二千一時俱發，洞甲穿中，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Rui arrayed chariots in formation; Dayan gathered cavalry and surrounded them; Rui with two thousand strong crossbows fired all at once, piercing armor through the middle; killed and wounded were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Rui arrayed chariots in formation; Dayan gathered cavalry and surrounded them; Rui with two thousand strong crossbows fired all at once, piercing armor; killed and wounded were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 矢貫大眼右臂，大眼退走。

translations.literal: An arrow pierced Dayan's right arm; Dayan withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow pierced Dayan's right arm; Dayan withdrew and fled.

sentences.zh: 明旦，英自帥眾來戰，睿乘素木輿，執白角如意以麾軍。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Ying himself led the masses to battle; Rui rode a plain wooden litter, holding a white-horn ruyi scepter to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Ying himself led his troops to battle; Rui rode in a plain wooden litter, holding a white-horn ruyi scepter to command the army.

sentences.zh: 一日數合，英乃退。

translations.literal: In one day they joined battle several times; Ying then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They fought several engagements in one day; Ying then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏師復夜來攻城，飛矢雨集。

translations.literal: The Wei army again came by night to attack the city; flying arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army again came by night to attack the city; arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 睿子黯請下城以避箭，睿不許。

translations.literal: Rui's son An asked to leave the wall to avoid arrows; Rui did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's son An asked to leave the wall to avoid the arrows; Rui refused.

sentences.zh: 軍中驚，睿於城上厲聲呵之，乃定。

translations.literal: The army was alarmed; Rui on the wall shouted sternly at them, and they then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The army panicked; Rui on the wall shouted sternly at them, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 牧人過淮北伐芻稿者，皆為楊大眼所略，曹景宗募勇敢士千餘人，於大眼城南數里築壘，大眼來攻，景宗擊卻之。

translations.literal: Herdsmen who crossed the Huai north to cut fodder were all plundered by Yang Dayan; Cao Jingzong recruited more than a thousand brave men and built ramparts several li south of Dayan's city; Dayan came to attack and Jingzong drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Herdsmen who crossed the Huai north to cut fodder were all plundered by Yang Dayan; Cao Jingzong recruited more than a thousand brave men and built ramparts several li south of Dayan's camp; Dayan attacked and Jingzong drove him back.

sentences.zh: 壘成，使別將趙草守之，有抄掠者，皆為草所獲，是後始得縱芻牧。

translations.literal: When the ramparts were complete, he had Separate Commander Zhao Cao defend them; any raiders were all captured by Cao; thereafter they could at last let herds graze freely.
translations.idiomatic: When the ramparts were complete, he had Separate Commander Zhao Cao defend them; any raiders were captured by Cao; thereafter they could at last let their herds graze freely.

sentences.zh: 上命景宗等豫裝高艦，使與魏橋等，為火攻之計。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jingzong and others to prepare tall ships in advance, making them equal to Wei's bridges, for a plan of fire attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jingzong and others to prepare tall ships in advance, matching Wei's bridges in height, for a fire attack.

sentences.zh: 令景宗與睿各攻一橋：睿攻其南，景宗攻其北。

translations.literal: He ordered Jingzong and Rui each to attack one bridge: Rui the south, Jingzong the north.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingzong and Rui each to attack one bridge: Rui the south, Jingzong the north.

sentences.zh: 三月，淮水瀑漲六七尺。

translations.literal: In the third month the Huai suddenly rose six or seven feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Huai suddenly rose six or seven feet.

sentences.zh: 睿使馮道根與廬江太守裴邃、秦郡太守李文釗等乘鬥艦競發，擊魏洲上軍盡殪。

translations.literal: Rui had Feng Daogen with Pei Sui, Administrator of Lujiang, Li Wenzhao, Administrator of Qin commandery, and others ride tower ships in competing advance and attack; the Wei army on the isle was all slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had Feng Daogen with Pei Sui, Administrator of Lujiang, Li Wenzhao, Administrator of Qin commandery, and others ride tower ships in a racing advance; the Wei army on the isle was annihilated.

sentences.zh: 別以小船載草，灌之以膏，從而焚其橋。

translations.literal: Separately small boats carried grass, poured fat over it, and then burned their bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Small boats carried grass, poured fat over it, and then set fire to the bridges.

sentences.zh: 風怒火盛，煙塵晦冥，敢死之士，拔柵斫橋，水又漂疾，倏忽之間，橋柵俱盡。

translations.literal: Wind and flame were fierce; smoke and dust darkened the sky; death-daring warriors pulled palisades and hewed bridges; the water also ran swift; in an instant bridges and palisades were all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and flame raged; smoke blotted out the sky; death-daring warriors pulled palisades and hewed bridges; the current ran swift; in an instant bridges and palisades were all gone.

sentences.zh: 道根等皆身自搏戰，軍人奮勇，呼聲動天地，無不一當百，魏軍大潰。

translations.literal: Daogen and others all fought in person; soldiers exerted courage; cries shook heaven and earth; none did not match a hundred; the Wei army was greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Daogen and others all fought in person; the soldiers fought with fury; their cries shook heaven and earth; each man fought as a hundred; the Wei army was routed.

sentences.zh: 英見橋絕，脫身棄城走，大眼亦燒營去，諸壘相次土崩，悉棄其器甲爭投水，死者十餘萬，斬首亦如之。

translations.literal: Ying saw the bridges cut and cast off his body, abandoned the city and fled; Dayan also burned his camp and left; the ramparts collapsed in succession like earthen walls; all cast off weapons and armor and strove to throw themselves into the water; the dead were more than a hundred thousand; heads cut off were likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: Ying saw the bridges cut and fled, abandoning the city; Dayan also burned his camp and left; the fortifications collapsed one after another; all cast off weapons and armor and threw themselves into the water; the dead numbered more than a hundred thousand; heads cut off were likewise countless.

sentences.zh: 睿遣報昌義之，義之悲喜，不暇答語，但叫曰：「更生！

translations.literal: Rui sent word to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi was joyful and sorrowful, with no leisure to reply, only crying: "Reborn!
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent word to Chang Yizhi; Yizhi was overcome with joy and grief, with no leisure to reply, only crying: "Reborn!

sentences.zh: 更生！」

translations.literal: Reborn!"
translations.idiomatic: Reborn!"

sentences.zh: 諸軍逐北至濊水上，英單騎入梁城，緣淮百餘里，屍相枕藉，生擒五萬人，收其資糧、器械山積，牛馬驢騾不可勝計。

translations.literal: The armies pursued north to the Wei River; Ying entered Liangcheng on a single horse; along the Huai for more than a hundred li corpses lay pillow on pillow; fifty thousand were captured alive; their stores, grain, and weapons were gathered in mountain piles; cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The armies pursued north to the Wei River; Ying fled alone on horseback into Liangcheng; along the Huai for more than a hundred li corpses lay piled upon corpses; fifty thousand were captured alive; stores, grain, and weapons were gathered in mountain heaps; cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 義之德景宗及睿，請二人共會，設錢二十萬，官賭之。

translations.literal: Yizhi was grateful to Jingzong and Rui and invited the two to meet together; he set out two hundred thousand cash for an official gambling match.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was grateful to Jingzong and Rui and invited the two to meet; he set out two hundred thousand cash for an official gambling match.

sentences.zh: 景宗擲得雉；

translations.literal: Jingzong threw and got the pheasant;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong threw and got the pheasant;

sentences.zh: 睿徐擲得盧，遽取一子反之，曰：「異事！」

translations.literal: Rui slowly threw and got the deer, then swiftly took one piece and reversed it, saying: "A strange thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Rui slowly threw and got the deer, then swiftly took one piece and reversed it, saying: "A strange thing!"

sentences.zh: 遂作塞。

translations.literal: He then made a blocking move.
translations.idiomatic: He then made a blocking move.

sentences.zh: 景宗與群帥爭先告捷，睿獨居後，世尤以此賢之。

translations.literal: Jingzong and the group of commanders vied to be first in reporting victory; Rui alone remained behind; the world especially deemed him worthy for this.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and the other commanders vied to be first in reporting victory; Rui alone remained behind; posterity especially esteemed him for this.

sentences.zh: 詔增景宗、睿爵邑，義之等受賞各有差。

translations.literal: An edict increased Jingzong's and Rui's fiefs and estates; Yizhi and others received rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict increased Jingzong's and Rui's fiefs and estates; Yizhi and others received rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己酉，以江州刺史王茂為尚書右僕射，安成王秀為江州刺史。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiyou Wang Mao, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and the Prince of Ancheng, Xiu, was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiyou Wang Mao, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and the Prince of Ancheng, Xiu, was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秀將發，主者求堅船以為齋舫，秀曰：「吾豈愛財而不愛士乎！」

translations.literal: When Xiu was about to depart, the steward sought sturdy boats for his vegetarian galley; Xiu said: "How could I love wealth and not love gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was about to depart, the steward sought sturdy boats for his vegetarian galley; Xiu said: "How could I love wealth and not love my men!"

sentences.zh: 乃以堅者給參佐，下者載齋物。

translations.literal: He then gave the sturdy ones to his staff and the inferior ones to carry vegetarian supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave the sturdy boats to his staff and used the inferior ones to carry vegetarian supplies.

sentences.zh: 既而遭風，齋舫遂破。

translations.literal: Afterward they met wind and the vegetarian galley was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they met a storm and the vegetarian galley was wrecked.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以臨川王宏為驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，建安王偉為揚州刺史，右光祿大夫沈約為尚書左僕射，左僕射王瑩為中軍將軍。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, was made General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies; the Prince of Jian'an, Wei, was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Shen Yue, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wang Ying, Left Vice Director, was made General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, was made General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies; the Prince of Jian'an, Wei, was appointed Inspector of Yangzhou; Shen Yue, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wang Ying, Left Vice Director, was appointed General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙午，馮翊等七郡叛，降魏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingwu seven commanderies including Fenyang rebelled and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingwu seven commanderies including Fenyang rebelled and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁亥，以尚書右僕射王茂為中軍將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai Wang Mao, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai Wang Mao, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊子，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuzi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 魏有司奏：「中山王英經算失圖，齊王蕭寶寅等守橋不固，皆處以極法。」

translations.literal: Wei officials memorialized: "The Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, miscalculated and lost his plan; the Prince of Qi, Xiao Baoyin, and others did not firmly hold the bridges—all should be punished by the extreme law."
translations.idiomatic: Wei officials memorialized: "The Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, miscalculated and lost his plan; the Prince of Qi, Xiao Baoyin, and others failed to hold the bridges—all should be punished by death."

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔英、寶寅免死，除名為民，楊大眼徙營州為兵。

translations.literal: On jihai an edict spared Ying and Baoyin from death, struck their names and made them commoners, and banished Yang Dayan to Yingzhou as a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai an edict spared Ying and Baoyin from death, struck their names from the rolls and made them commoners, and banished Yang Dayan to Yingzhou as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 以中護軍李崇為征南將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Chong, General of the Central Guard, was made General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, General of the Central Guard, was appointed General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇多事產業。

translations.literal: Chong was much engaged in estates and enterprises.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was much engaged in estates and business ventures.

sentences.zh: 征南長史狄道辛琛屢諫不從，遂相糾舉。

translations.literal: Xin Chen of Didao, Chief Clerk of Campaign South, repeatedly remonstrated but was not followed; he then mutually impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chen of Didao, Chief Clerk of Campaign South, repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded; he then impeached him.

sentences.zh: 詔並不問。

translations.literal: An edict inquired into neither.
translations.idiomatic: An edict took no action against either.

sentences.zh: 崇因置酒謂琛曰：「長史後必為刺史，但不知得上佐何如人耳。」

translations.literal: Chong then set out wine and said to Chen: "Chief Clerk, you will surely become an inspector later, but I do not know what sort of man your senior assistant will be."
translations.idiomatic: Chong then set out wine and said to Chen: "Chief Clerk, you will surely become an inspector later, but I do not know what sort of man your senior assistant will be."

sentences.zh: 琛曰：「若萬一叨忝，得一方正長史，朝夕聞過，是所願也。」

translations.literal: Chen said: "If by the one-in-ten-thousand chance I am favored with appointment, to get a square and upright chief clerk and hear of faults morning and evening—that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Chen said: "If by chance I am favored with appointment, to get an upright chief clerk and hear of my faults morning and evening—that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 崇有慚色。

translations.literal: Chong had a shamefaced look.
translations.idiomatic: Chong looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 九月，己亥，魏以司空高陽王雍為太尉，尚書令廣陽王嘉為司空。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jihai Wei made the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, Minister of Works, Grand Minister, and Guangyang Wang Jia, Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jihai Wei made the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong, Grand Minister, and Guangyang Wang Jia, Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏開斜谷舊道。

translations.literal: On jiazi Wei opened the old road of Xiegu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Wei opened the old road of Xiegu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬寅，以五兵尚書徐勉為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renyin Xu Mian, Director of the Secretariat for the Five Armies, was made Director of the Secretariat for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renyin Xu Mian, Director of the Secretariat for the Five Armies, was appointed Director of the Secretariat for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 勉精力過人，雖文案填積，坐客充滿，應對如流，手不停筆。

translations.literal: Mian's energy surpassed others; though documents piled up and seated guests filled the room, he responded like flowing water and his hand never stopped the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's energy surpassed others; though documents piled up and guests filled the room, he responded effortlessly and his hand never stopped writing.

sentences.zh: 又該綜百氏，皆為避諱。

translations.literal: He also mastered the hundred schools, all for the sake of taboo avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: He also mastered the hundred schools of thought, all for the sake of taboo avoidance.

sentences.zh: 嘗與門人夜集，客虞暠求詹事五官，勉正色曰：「今夕止可談風月，不可及公事。」

translations.literal: Once he gathered at night with his disciples; the guest Yu Gao sought the Five Offices of the Household Administration; Mian with stern countenance said: "This evening we may only discuss wind and moon—we may not touch public business."
translations.idiomatic: Once he gathered at night with his disciples; the guest Yu Gao sought an office in the Household Administration; Mian with stern countenance said: "This evening we may only discuss poetry and nature—we may not touch public business."

sentences.zh: 時人鹹服其無私。

translations.literal: People of the time all submitted to his lack of selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time all admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙丑，以臨川王宏為司徒、行太子太傅，尚書左僕射沈約為尚書令、行太子少傅，吏部尚書昂昂為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on yichou the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, was made Minister of Works and Acting Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Shen Yue, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat and Acting Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Angang, Director of the Secretariat for Personnel, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yichou the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, was made Minister of Works and Acting Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Shen Yue, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat and Acting Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Wang Ying, Director of the Secretariat for Personnel, was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，魏皇后于氏殂。

translations.literal: On dingmao the Empress of Wei, née Yu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Empress of Wei, née Yu, died.

sentences.zh: 是時高貴嬪有寵而妒，高肇勢傾中外，後暴疾而殂，人皆歸咎高氏。

translations.literal: At this time the Noble Consort was favored yet jealous; Gao Zhao's power tilted inside and outside; the empress died of sudden illness and people all blamed the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Noble Consort was favored yet jealous; Gao Zhao's power dominated court and realm; the empress died of sudden illness and people all blamed the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 宮禁事秘，莫能詳也。

translations.literal: Palace matters were secret; none could know in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Palace matters were secret; none could know the details.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以光祿大夫夏侯詳為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jiashen Xiahou Xiang, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Xiahou Xiang, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，魏葬順皇后於永泰陵。

translations.literal: On yiyou Wei buried the Shun Empress at Yongtai Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Wei buried the Shun Empress at Yongtai Tomb.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙辰，豐城景公夏侯詳卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingchen Xiahou Xiang, Duke of Fengcheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingchen Xiahou Xiang, Duke of Fengcheng, died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏淮陽鎮都軍主常邕和以城來降。

translations.literal: On yichou Chang Yonghe, Army Commander of the Huaiyang garrison in Wei, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Chang Yonghe, Army Commander of the Huaiyang garrison in Wei, surrendered the city.
